briefs.title: Nationwide Ground Stop: What We Know and What Could Explain It
briefs.bluf: As of about 7pm ET the nationwide ground stop is still in place. The FAA is releasing some flights as its high altitude control centers recover. Officials call it a telecom outage and say they see no sign of an attack. Bloomberg reports the FBI is looking at a software update. The evidence so far leans toward a technical failure, which is how 11 of the 13 big air traffic outages Brief reviewed since 2001 turned out. Three things do not fit neatly yet. Several distant centers lost radios at once. The FAA's new AI routing tool went nationwide three days ago. Its telecom network is also mid handover to a new contractor. No group has claimed it and nothing points to a staged event, but no cause is confirmed yet.

1960 scientific paper, so it marks the start of something larger. the simpsons predicted a "great blackout" in november, and the nov 17 national emergency alert test is the trigger for it. the pentagon plan for bases to run 90 days off the grid shows officials know a long blackout or attack is coming. governments are issuing synchronized emergency warnings, which signals a coordinated plan or known coming crisis. the faa's new ai planning system, smart, caused or contributed to the outage. the official story of a telecom outage is hiding a cyberattack or other attack. the global microsoft outage on nov 12 and the faa failure on nov 13 are linked, possibly through ai agents or a common attack. nvidia chief jensen huang's resignation the day before signals insider knowledge of an ai related failure or crisis. the outage, or a coming bigger one, will be used as a pretext for emergency powers or martial law. the outage could serve as a pretext for renewed war with iran, or was iranian retaliation. the real story is underfunding, staff shortages and rushed privatized ai, not a plot. the new ai air traffic tool (smart) caused or triggered the outage. the flight stop, a national weather radar outage and a microsoft outage are a coordinated attack on infrastructure. controllers are in a dispute with the faa and military units were put on alert. the 1402 day gap since the last nationwide stop carries a hidden message. a foreign or unknown cyberattack is under way against us air traffic control. it was not truly nationwide and was really a chicago fault. leadership failure is to blame, either the prior administration or current officials.

briefs.title: Catch Up: Colom Wins Mississippi, Abu Dhabi Ends in a Prisoner Deal, US Jets Leave a UK Base
briefs.bluf: This edition covers Tuesday through Thursday because three mornings were missed. AP called Mississippi's Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom, and local outlets report Hyde-Smith conceded. The Abu Dhabi talks ended Wednesday with a deal in principle on a big prisoner swap, but no movement on territory. The US pulled tanker planes out of a British base after an Iranian threat, the clearest sign yet that the war's risk reaches Europe. The House shelved the move to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth, 211 to 204.
briefs._s: catch up: colom wins mississippi, abu dhabi ends in a prisoner deal, us jets leave a uk base this edition covers tuesday through thursday because three mornings were missed. ap called mississippi's senate race for democrat scott colom, and local outlets report hyde-smith conceded. the abu dhabi talks ended wednesday with a deal in principle on a big prisoner swap, but no movement on territory. the us pulled tanker planes out of a british base after an iranian threat, the clearest sign yet that the war's risk reaches europe. the house shelved the move to impeach defense secretary hegseth, 211 to 204. ap calls mississippi's senate race for democrat scott colom the associated press called the race for scott colom, a democratic district attorney, over republican senator cindy hyde-smith. as of nov 12 at 5:54pm et, ap's count showed colom at 476,120 votes (49.3%) and hyde-smith at 470,179 (48.6%), with about 99% of votes estimated counted. those numbers may have changed since. mississippi free press and wlox pages carry headlines saying hyde-smith conceded and governor tate reeves commented, but we could not open those stories. experian says its data was never meant to check mississippi voters mississippi made more than 230,000 voter registrations inactive before election day, according to mississippi today reporting cited by newsweek. many of those voters had to cast affidavit ballots, which are provisional ballots checked later. experian, the credit bureau whose data was used in the roll cleanup, now says it has not worked for the state since early 2025. it also says its earlier work was not built to validate voter records. about 76% of mississippi's affidavit ballots were accepted by tuesday, november 10, counties had processed 15,547 affidavit ballots statewide and accepted about 76%, the secretary of state's office told wlox. tuesday was also the last day for mailed ballots to arrive and for affidavit voters to prove their identity at the clerk's office. in rankin county, a bipartisan committee reviews each ballot before it is opened, so nobody knows the voter's party during the check. house shelves hegseth impeachment, 211 to 204 on november 10 the house voted 211 to 204 to send impeachment articles against defense secretary pete hegseth to the judiciary committee. that move kills them for this congress. representative thomas massie, a kentucky republican who lost his primary, filed eight articles. they cover the iran war, a strike on an iranian school, boat strikes, the maduro capture, yemen and pressure on senator mark kelly. hegseth called them policy disagreements at his first pentagon press conference in six months. alaska senate count: peltola ahead, no ap call before ranked count as of nov 11 at 10:34pm et, ap had democrat mary peltola at 121,487 votes (48.9%). republican senator dan sullivan had 117,512 (47.3%), with about 86% counted. a second, unrelated candidate named daniel j. sullivan jr. had 4,100 votes. ap has not called the race and the count is not finished. these numbers may have changed since. alaska runs its ranked choice count on november 18. us pulls tanker planes out of a british base over an iran threat on monday the us air force flew at least 10 kc-135 refuelling tankers out of raf mildenhall in eastern england. they went to germany, spain and scotland, and osprey aircraft moved to nearby lakenheath. the wall street journal tied the move to a threat from iran, and both bases went to the second highest alert level. the us military would only say it moves aircraft for many reasons. another tanker hit near hormuz as an emirati state ship is damaged a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 19 nautical miles northeast of lima, oman, on november 10. the crew was safe, according to the uk maritime trade operations centre, a british navy desk that logs attacks on ships. the same afternoon a vessel run by adnoc, the uae state oil company's shipping arm, was damaged inside uae waters. nobody has claimed either attack. qatar says vance may meet iran's security chief in doha next week qatar's prime minister met president trump for 45 minutes and vice president jd vance separately in washington. turkey's intelligence chief ibrahim kalin then said qatar would host vance and iran's top security official mohsen rezaei the following week. tasnim, an iranian news agency close to the revolutionary guards, quoted an official denying any such meeting. the reported deal would ease the us naval blockade and free iranian funds in exchange for nuclear inspections and a reopened strait. iran's parliament weighs letting a non cleric run the spy ministry iran's parliament is preparing to debate a bill that would let someone who is not a cleric head the intelligence ministry for the first time. the same bill would let supreme leader mojtaba khamenei directly appoint the heads of two new bodies inside the ministry. every intelligence minister since the 1980s has been a cleric. iran reportedly names a quds force commander as its next envoy to baghdad iran has reportedly chosen abdolreza masgarian, a commander in the quds force, the revolutionary guards unit that runs allied militias abroad, as ambassador to iraq. he would replace mohammad kazem al-e sadegh. tehran has not confirmed it. the report came the same day iraqi prime minister ali al-zaidi was in tehran meeting iran's chief negotiator. new knesset sworn in as eisenkot's bloc moves to seize the speaker's chair israel's 26th knesset, the parliament, was sworn in on november 10 with no government in place. gadi eisenkot, a former army chief who leads the yashar party, has until december 6 to form one, extendable to december 20. his bloc gathered 67 signatures to force a vote next tuesday replacing speaker amir ohana, a netanyahu ally, with yashar's matan kahana. eisenkot's allies also filed bills for an october 7 state inquiry, prime minister term limits, and repeal of the judicial overhaul. liberman tells eisenkot to drop a government backed by arab parties avigdor liberman, leader of the secular nationalist yisrael beytenu party, demanded that eisenkot give up the idea of a minority government kept alive by arab parties. he says he can bring the ultra orthodox parties in instead. those parties have so far said they will not join an eisenkot government. united torah judaism wants written guarantees before any deal. raam's abbas reportedly ready to call hamas a terror group in the opening session, outgoing speaker ohana cited a ynet report about mansour abbas, head of the islamist arab party raam. it says abbas is willing to call hamas a terrorist group in talks with the anti netanyahu bloc. abbas stood for the national anthem while several arab lawmakers walked out. a united torah judaism lawmaker stood beside him. settlers burn machinery in beita and beat activists in qusra dozens of settlers burned excavators and stone cutting equipment in beita's industrial zone, south of nablus, on november 9. the report comes from palestinian security sources and the wafa agency. settlers also beat activists in qusra and used tear gas on farmers in beit al-roush near hebron. israeli media said the beita arson followed palestinians torching a vehicle near a settlement the day before. houthis claim a drone hit on saudi arabia's hormuz bypass pipeline at yanbu on november 11 the houthis, the iran aligned group that holds northern yemen, claimed a drone attack on a pumping station at yanbu. yanbu is the red sea end of saudi arabia's east west oil pipeline, the main route that lets saudi oil skip the strait of hormuz. saudi arabia reported a limited fire on that pipeline on november 9. the saudi led coalition says it downed cruise missiles, drones and two ballistic missiles aimed at riyadh the same day. strikes hit sanaa's gas and oil company sites as missiles hit coalition camps in aden strikes on november 10 set gas tanker trailers on fire at the al-mafzar station in northern sanaa. they also hit the houthi run yemen petroleum company headquarters, according to houthi media. the houthis blamed saudi arabia, which did not comment. on november 11 police sources told afp that missiles hit coalition camps in western and central aden, the seat of the saudi backed government. houthis close dozens of sanaa bakeries, raising bread shortage fears houthi authorities shut dozens of bakeries in sanaa on november 11, which local sources described as an extortion campaign, according to arab news. residents fear bread shortages. it comes as saudi strikes hit fuel sites in the city. un agencies warn over a million in lebanon face acute hunger the un food and agriculture organization, the world food programme and lebanon's agriculture ministry warned on november 11 that more than one million people face acute food insecurity. israeli strikes and shelling continued on the outskirts of southern towns including markaba, wadi al-saluki and al-jarmaq on november 9, with damage to farmland reported. mada masr editor's november 11 retrial: outcome not yet public lina attalah edits mada masr, egypt's best known independent news site. she was due for retrial on november 11 in a 2024 case that gave her one year in prison in absentia. no outcome had been reported in sources reachable for this edition. separately, supporters paid her 3 million pound fine, about $55,000, and the appeal against the order closing mada masr is set for november 25. the six person staff of matsadaash, a fact checking group, remain in pretrial detention. abu dhabi talks end with a prisoner swap deal and no breakthrough russia and ukraine agreed in principle on a large prisoner swap after two days of us mediated talks in abu dhabi. russian and us officials announced it on november 11. russian state news agency tass says the swap should happen in two to three weeks. russia's lead negotiator vladimir medinsky said the main topic was europe's future security system, with agreement on some points and not others. on territory he said every inch would return to russia. ukraine's negotiator david arakhamia said a deal by the end of the year is possible and wants europe at the next round. abu dhabi day one: talks center on a 1,000 for 1,000 prisoner swap ukrainian, russian and us negotiators met for about four hours in abu dhabi on november 10. it was their first three way meeting since february. zelensky said the russian side proposed swapping 1,000 prisoners each, maybe 1,500 each, and that us officials would carry the offer to moscow. he said territory came up but must be settled by leaders, not negotiators. russia brought the fsb officer kyiv accuses of plotting to kill budanov dmitry minaev runs the counterintelligence operations department of the fsb, russia's main security service. he sits on russia's delegation as one of six experts. ukrainian sources told the wall street journal his department was behind a failed attempt on kyrylo budanov, now zelensky's chief of staff and also at the table. evan gershkovich, the freed wsj reporter, has said minaev escorted prisoners at the 2024 swap. us reportedly floated redrawing donbas borders so both sides can claim victory meduza's live coverage, citing the economist, says us negotiators raised changing the official borders of the donetsk and luhansk regions. the idea would let russia say it took the regions in full without ukraine formally giving up land. the same feed cites axios saying washington lifted sanctions on russian diesel sales. zelensky, speaking from denmark, said trading donbas for guarantees is unacceptable without nato style protection. refinery war forces russian fuel rationing as ukraine's grid loses 14 plants ukrainian drones hit ten russian oil sites in 11 days, most recently the kirishi refinery near st petersburg on november 9. rosneft, the state oil company, capped sales at 30 liters per car at city stations. russia carried out more than 130 attacks on ukraine's power system in a week, and at least 14 of 38 ukrainian plants are out. kyiv says it stopped honoring a white house request to spare refineries on october 30. moscow wants europe's security rules settled before the ukraine war russia's foreign minister sergei lavrov said a broad european security framework should be defined before the war itself is resolved, and he rejected a truce. deputy foreign minister sergei ryabkov, who handles arms control, joined the delegation and said it was too early to judge the meeting. zelensky set the opposite order: stop the war, then guarantees for ukraine, then wider european security. new: dublin summit will only sketch europe's putin envoy, decision in december eu leaders meet informally in dublin on november 13. they will discuss the profile and mandate of someone to speak for europe in peace talks, with names coming later. italy's giorgia meloni forced the debate with a letter warning europe risks irrelevance. council president antónio costa agreed but insists the eu's own institutions must represent it under the treaties. eu, us, nato and kyiv sign a joint line before facing russia before the three way session, the eu, france, germany, italy, the uk, ukraine, the us and nato met in abu dhabi and issued a joint statement. it says any deal must respect ukraine's borders and give it credible security guarantees. it also says a strong nato stays central to defending europe and north america, and that talks should later widen to include europe. europe's team waited outside the room in abu dhabi the eu sent a joint team led by björn seibert, chief of staff to commission head ursula von der leyen. anna-maria boura, a foreign policy adviser to costa. security advisers from france, germany and the uk also came. an eu official said europeans would not be in the room. kremlin spokesman dmitry peskov said the talks were three way only. kallas: europe already has security rules, russia signed them in 1994 eu foreign policy chief kaja kallas said russia is only pretending to negotiate, pointing to its air campaign on ukrainian cities and power plants. she rejected moscow's call for new european security rules. she said the 1994 budapest memorandum, in which russia, the us and the uk promised to respect ukraine's borders, already is that framework. france's jean-noël barrot said there can be no european security talks before a ceasefire. beijing extends its rare earth pause by just two months china's commerce ministry extended its suspension of some export controls to january 10, 2027. the pause had been due to expire november 10. it covers five rare earths, processing technology, some lithium battery and graphite materials, and foreign products containing chinese rare earths. controls from april 2025 on seven other rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, stay in force. beijing confirms talks on a trump, putin and xi meeting at apec china's foreign ministry spokesperson guo jiakun said china is in contact with the relevant parties about a meeting of the three leaders. he was responding to a wall street journal report. that report said xi would only join if the talks allow open discussion of arms control. guo gave no further detail. no xi and takaichi meeting expected at the shenzhen summit japanese officials told jiji press there will be no summit with xi on the sidelines of apec in shenzhen on november 18 and 19. beijing still demands that prime minister sanae takaichi retract her 2025 remark that a taiwan crisis could threaten japan's survival. china rejected a japanese offer to reaffirm the 1972 joint statement instead. asked on november 11, beijing's spokesperson only said china had made its position clear more than once. najib goes home under house arrest after a fresh court order former malaysian prime minister najib razak left kajang prison and reached his kuala lumpur home at about 9:27 pm on november 10. high court judge aslam zainuddin replaced the november 6 order with a new one based on the conditional royal pardon. the attorney general's office had held up the earlier order, saying its wording needed clarifying. najib can serve the rest of his sentence at home until august 23, 2028. myanmar army says it took an opposition regional headquarters near yangon state newspaper myanma alinn said the army seized a regional command headquarters of the national unity government and 10 other bases. the national unity government is the shadow government formed by lawmakers the army ousted in 2021. the jungle site is on the mon and bago border, about 120 km from yangon. a karen national liberation army battalion base was also reportedly taken. ap could not confirm the claim. japan gives vietnam its first security aid and a rare earth pact prime minister sanae takaichi hosted to lam, vietnam's communist party chief and president, in tokyo. they agreed to deepen security cooperation and to cooperate on rare earth metals to make supply chains more resilient. japan will send its first peacekeeping equipment to vietnam under its official security assistance program, which gives defense gear to friendly militaries. they also discussed the south china sea, but announced nothing on it. premier li, not xi, carries beijing's trade pitch to thailand and manila beijing said premier li qiang will visit thailand from november 13 to 15. he will then attend the china and asean summit in manila on november 15 and 16. asean is the association of southeast asian nations. china wants an upgraded free trade agreement with asean, called version 3.0, brought into force as soon as possible. new zealand's opportunity party drops its basic income demand in talks with luxon prime minister christopher luxon met qiulae wong, leader of the centrist opportunity party, on november 9. his coalition holds a majority of just two seats on preliminary counts. special votes, about a seventh of the total and usually left leaning, are counted by november 27. opportunity's minimum demands are a stronger competition watchdog, tighter lobbying rules and donation caps. its universal basic income and land tax ideas are not on the list. us formally serves india in a lawsuit naming doval over a murder plot the us state department served india by diplomatic note in a civil suit filed by gurpatwant singh pannun. pannun is a us based sikh separatist who says indian officials plotted to kill him. the suit names national security adviser ajit doval and former foreign spy chief samant goel. india's foreign ministry called the lawsuit frivolous. fake court orders were used to block 129 websites in india reuters reported that india's telecom department ordered 129 betting websites blocked based on two high court orders that appear to be forged. the allahabad high court filed a police complaint on november 6. separately, delhi police opened a case over forged police notices asking x to block two digital rights groups. police traced the notices to a 17 year old in srinagar, and x told a court it would not take the accounts down. indian inflation tops 6% for the first time in two years retail inflation rose to 6.09% in october from 5.5% in september. that is above the upper limit of the reserve bank of india's target band. food inflation reached 8.9%, led by onions, garlic and ginger. assam court says pan and voter cards alone do not prove citizenship the gauhati high court upheld a foreigners tribunal order declaring a woman a foreigner. foreigners tribunals are special courts in assam that decide who is an illegal migrant. the judges said a tax id card and a voter card are issued on self declaration, so they need supporting records. the court also canceled her interim bail. norwegian journalist says india canceled her visa without a reason helle lyng svendsen says india's embassy in oslo told her not to travel to a summit in hyderabad. she says her visa was then canceled with no reason given. the editors guild of india asked the government to explain and reverse it. the government had not commented. lula leaves for cop31 and manila, freezing his cabinet picks president lula flew to turkey on november 9 for the cop31 climate summit, then goes to manila for the asean summit of southeast asian nations. he returns november 16. he pushed the choice of a 2027 finance minister and a fiscal adjustment package until after the trip. allies say he wants names settled by november 25 and the full team announced by december 5. lula wants to tie lawmakers' budget money to their votes brazilian lawmakers steer a large slice of the federal budget through 'emendas', amendments that fund projects back home. lula wants to win back sway over part of that money and release it only to those who vote with him. that collides with the budget control now held by chamber speaker hugo motta and senate president davi alcolumbre. no party has agreed to it. new: parties that backed flávio bolsonaro still bid for lula's ministries republicanos, união brasil and pp endorsed flávio bolsonaro, the former president's son, in the runoff. all three still want cabinet posts. psd is asking for three ministries, including agriculture, and mdb wants to keep its current share. the government now asks each party for a policy plan and an estimate of the votes it can deliver. a stronger opposition senate keeps lula's senators out of the cabinet bolsonaro's liberal party (pl) will hold 29 senate seats and the novo party 3. lula's allies are weighing keeping senators rui costa, wellington dias and renan filho in the chamber instead of naming them ministers. renan filho was reportedly sounded out to lead the government's bench. senate president davi alcolumbre faces challenges from rogério marinho (pl) and tereza cristina (pp). us report: $12 billion in venezuelan oil money spent under us control a 53 page state department report to congress, dated october 29 and audited by kpmg, covers a us held 'venezuela custody account'. it took in about $12.26 billion from january 3 to september 30, and 98.7% was paid out. food and consumer goods took 35.75%, administrative services 23%, agriculture 12.5% and health 5.68%. the money came from oil, gold, minerals and fertilizer sales by approved firms. venezuela's assembly opens the power grid to private generators the national assembly, led by jorge rodríguez, unanimously approved a reform on november 10 letting private firms generate electricity and sell it at a set tariff. it follows new oil and mining laws pushed by acting president delcy rodríguez. opposition deputy antonio ecarri backed it, citing the collapse of the state power company. blackouts hit much of the country daily. new: venezuela's army sweeps apure for armed groups, never naming the eln venezuela's armed forces command said on november 12 that units are searching river and forest areas of apure state for camps and hidden airstrips of 'irregular groups'. the foreign ministry asked for channels with colombia to share information. neither statement named the eln, the colombian guerrilla group venezuela bombed days earlier. two piaroa indigenous people were reported killed in eln and farc dissident clashes in bolívar state on november 11. eln frees two investigators after 533 days, then seizes a mayor's wife the eln guerrilla released two agents of the prosecutor's investigative unit (cti) in arauca on november 12, held since may 2025. a day earlier, armed men believed to be eln abducted nancy gómez, wife of the mayor of uribia in la guajira. the group also holds army lt. maría camila pantoja, taken november 4, and sent proof she is alive. president abelardo de la espriella ordered a full deployment to find gómez. fitch puts paraguay's rating on watch after the ueno collapse on november 11 fitch put paraguay's bb+ rating on watch for a cut and dropped its positive outlook. ueno, the sixth largest bank, held about $2.9 billion in deposits, and about $2.1 billion of it is uninsured. roughly $900 million of that belongs to public bodies, including the pension institute and the binational dams. fitch puts the possible rescue cost at 1.5% of gdp, about $900 million. paraguay's pension fund may dip into savings to pay november pensions an internal note at ips, paraguay's social security institute, dated november 9 proposes using about 784 billion guaraníes of investment returns to cover november and december payouts. about 411.8 billion guaraníes of its operating cash is frozen at ueno. the note awaits a legal opinion, and ips has not commented publicly. the fund already takes in about $72.6 million a month and pays out $73.6 million. salvadoran helicopters hit a haitian gang base, about 20 reported dead president nayib bukele said on november 10 that his forces destroyed the headquarters of the 400 mawozo gang in croix-des-bouquets, near port-au-prince. he posted video of helicopters firing on the site, and about 20 people were reported killed. haitian police say they led the raid with salvadoran support. amnesty international asked both governments to publish the deployment agreement and allow independent investigations. ortega reappears frail after 68 days as managua rejects trump's envoy daniel ortega appeared on november 9 at a tribute to sandinista founder carlos fonseca, his first public outing since september 2. he walked slowly and gave no speech, and the government has never explained his absences. the independent outlet confidencial counts 11 appearances this year, against a usual 26. nicaragua also refused natasha franceschi, trump's ambassador pick, and washington recalled its chargé d'affaires elias baumann. sudan lifts its 20 month ban on kenyan tea sudan's army led government ended a ban on kenyan tea imports on november 11. it had imposed the ban about 20 months ago because nairobi hosted leaders of the rapid support forces (rsf), the paramilitary it is fighting. the rsf and its allies had signed their parallel government charter in nairobi. sudanese lawyers doubt the army really arrested icc fugitive haroun ahmed haroun is a former leader of omar al bashir's ruling party wanted by the international criminal court for darfur crimes. ap and reuters reported on november 8 that the army detained him after a podcast interview. on november 10 and 11 sudanese politicians, activists and the emergency lawyers rights group said there is still no independent proof or official confirmation of the arrest. hackers drain kordofan traders' accounts on sudan's main payment app more than 50 traders and customers in kordofan say millions of sudanese pounds vanished from their bankak accounts. bankak is the mobile banking app of the bank of khartoum. it became the main way sudanese pay for things after cash ran short during the war. congo military court sentences at least 66 soldiers to death for fleeing a military court in walikale, north kivu, sentenced at least 66 soldiers to death for cowardice, mutiny and disobeying orders. they were arrested october 20 after reportedly fleeing fighting with the frn, a rebel coalition that includes m23 and is now led by former president joseph kabila. rfi counts 381 death sentences among 507 soldiers convicted since early 2025, though congo has carried out no formal executions. cameroon sets twice delayed elections for february 7 president paul biya, 93, signed a decree on november 9 setting legislative and local elections for february 7, 2027. lawmakers' terms were stretched to december 20 and local councilors' terms to february 28. the party of opposition figure issa tchiroma bakary, now in exile in the gambia, remains suspended. rights lawyers say up to 2,000 people were detained after last year's election protests. anc and rivals weigh a bloc to keep the da out of johannesburg the democratic alliance (da) won the most votes in johannesburg, about 35%, but no majority. bloomberg sources say the anc, actionsa, jacob zuma's mk party and the economic freedom fighters are discussing an alliance. the goal is to make actionsa's herman mashaba mayor and shut out the da's helen zille. actionsa chair michael beaumont met anc secretary general fikile mbalula on november 8, and parties have 14 days from the results to form councils. nine zimbabweans arrested in johannesburg over russia ukraine war recruitment south african police arrested nine zimbabweans aged 20 to 26, five at or tambo airport and four at a hotel. they are charged under south africa's law against unauthorized foreign military service. police have not said which side they meant to fight for or who recruited them, and zimbabwe says some of its citizens recruited for russia have died. nearly 64,000 nigerians have fled into niger this year the un refugee agency (unhcr) says nearly 64,000 people fled northern nigeria for niger this year to escape islamist militants and armed gangs. most went to diffa and tahoua, and more than two thirds of those in diffa are children. only about 5% are formally registered. unicef says drone strikes on sudan's power stations cut off water and care the un children's agency (unicef) said on november 11 that drone attacks on sudan's power stations are cutting children off from water, schools and basic care. drought is making it worse. its headline called the attacks unlike anything sudan has seen before. in rabak, capital of white nile state, residents have had no electricity for 14 straight days after a drone hit the mashkour substation, and prices have soared. poland says the pentagon backs a permanent us base poland will fund poland's defense minister, władysław kosiniak-kamysz, said defense secretary pete hegseth gave a green light to a permanent us base at a november 10 pentagon meeting. poland offers to pay the building costs, estimated at $3.8 to 4.4 billion, for about 5,000 us troops and up to 25,000 people in total. the white house is expected to decide in early december. all four candidate cities sit west of the vistula river, far from the russian and belarusian borders. nato now uses ukrainian forces as the enemy in its drills adm. pierre vandier, who heads nato's command for future warfare, said the alliance hides ukrainian troops and ukrainian sea drones inside its exercises to play the opposing side. the aim is to force nato units to adapt to cheap drone warfare. ukraine's defense ministry claims its team beat nato navies in all five scenarios at a 2025 exercise off portugal. breaking defense could not verify that claim. eu agrees its 2027 defense budget as four states refuse to lend to ukraine the european parliament and eu governments agreed the bloc's 2027 defense and security budget of about $3.4 billion. it sets aside €650 million for ukraine from a €90 billion loan pool, while zelensky has asked for at least €70 billion more. hungary, slovakia, the czech republic and bulgaria have opted out of the lending. german chancellor friedrich merz reportedly threatened to block the next long term eu budget if members refuse to chip in. ukrainian missile maker wants spacex coverage beyond ukraine's borders fire point, a ukrainian arms company, wants spacex's military satellite network, called starshield, to work beyond ukrainian territory. the contract reportedly ends in mid 2027. the firm says its own workaround gives only 15 to 20% of starshield's capability, a claim not verified. its fp-9 missile is listed with a range of up to 850 km. oil bounces off a ten week low after trump says no iran deal is needed brent crude, the global oil benchmark, hit a ten week low of about $91.5 a barrel on november 10. by november 12 it was back near $96 after president trump said the us no longer needs a deal with iran. an iranian official also ruled out sending enriched nuclear material abroad. hotter october inflation lifts december rate hike odds to 87% us consumer prices rose 0.4% in october, above the 0.3% forecast. core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%. futures markets now put the chance of a federal reserve hike in december at 87%, up from about 77% a week earlier. the fed already raised rates in september for the first time in three years. gold slips toward $4,000 during a war, far below its january record gold traded near $4,050 an ounce on november 10, down from a record above $5,000 in late january. rising rate hike odds pushed it lower because gold pays no interest. bitcoin also slid, to about $74,000. us gas falls below $4, but refiners put off maintenance to get here the aaa national average for regular gas fell to $3.98 a gallon on november 10. demand dropped after the summer driving season and the switch back to standard time. many us refineries also delayed routine maintenance this year to keep fuel flowing, and that work will soon come due. saudi output jumps 26% as gulf crude finds ways around hormuz saudi arabia reported a 26% rise in october oil output, and iraq also raised production. shipments still depend on other routes and naval escorts. us crude stocks rose by about 4.66 million barrels in the week to november 6, the biggest build since august. senate advances a 417 page permitting bill as trump vows no wind permits on november 9 the senate advanced a bill to speed permits for data centers, pipelines and power lines. two republicans and two democrats sponsor it, and trump urged every senator to back it. trump also said his administration will not approve wind turbine permits, which politico calls a key part of the bill. exxon reaches a preliminary deal to return to venezuela exxonmobil, the largest us oil company, has reached a preliminary deal to go back into venezuela, the new york times reported on november 9. exxon was pushed out of venezuela nearly two decades ago when its projects were nationalized. war, not climate policy, pushed global emissions down this year the global carbon budget, an annual scientific tally of carbon dioxide, projects fossil emissions of 32.8 billion tonnes in 2026. that is 0.4% lower than 2025. oil emissions fell nearly 2% as the gulf and ukraine wars drove up fuel prices, while coal emissions rose about 0.6%. pentagon lends $450 million to space firms to cover a coming launch gap the pentagon's office of strategic capital, a lending arm set up in 2022, gave conditional $150 million loans each to rocket lab, stoke space and leolabs. rocket lab and stoke build rockets, and leolabs tracks objects in orbit with radar. the loans target a projected shortfall of at least 150 launches through 2030, after spacex stops flying commercial payloads on its falcon 9 rocket in 2028. the office is asking for $20 billion in mandatory funding for 2027. un nature fund for genetic data has raised under $11,000 the cali fund was set up at the 2024 un biodiversity summit so companies that profit from genetic data drawn from nature would pay into it. the financial times reported it has raised less than $11,000. china hands carbon data to its statistics bureau to fight fake numbers china ordered its national bureau of statistics to oversee carbon emission surveys, the south china morning post reported. beijing frames it as part of a push to stamp out fake data using modern technology. cape coral's new council members begin orientation newly elected cape coral council members started orientation on november 11, with a second session friday, november 13. they join mayor elect rick erickson, a retired green beret. the new council takes office as amendment 3, the voter approved property tax cut, starts squeezing city budgets. more than 44,000 tickets issued for passing stopped school buses the cape coral breeze reports more than 44,000 citations issued to drivers who passed stopped school buses. the breeze homepage summary did not say which agency issued them or over what period. epoch times: doj has not confirmed huang's affair partner was a spy the epoch times is a right leaning paper tied to the falun gong movement. on nov 12 it quoted todd blanche, a senior justice department official. he said the department has not confirmed the woman in the nvidia affair was a chinese spy. the headline now calls jensen huang the former nvidia ceo. the woman is alice huang (no relation), a chinese executive at megaspeed, a big nvidia customer that the justice department is pursuing in a criminal chip case. bannon tells his audience to stop calling the midterms stolen steve bannon, the former trump strategist who hosts the war room show, told viewers on nov 7 that people should stop complaining about a stolen election. he said they must face the fact that the other side is taking the house and senate. he still raised questions about 19 million extra voters and said the party must learn how turnout hit presidential year levels. media matters, a liberal watchdog, posted the clip on nov 9. kucinich: 11 absent democrats let hegseth dodge an impeachment vote dennis kucinich, a former ohio congressman, wrote in consortium news on nov 12 that the house sent rep. thomas massie's impeachment resolution against defense secretary pete hegseth to committee by 211 to 204. he says 11 democrats, including nancy pelosi, were absent. had they voted no, the referral would have failed and the house would have voted on impeachment itself. new: 12 senators push to strip israel defense integration from defense bills antiwar.com reporter dave decamp reported on nov 12 that 12 senators wrote to leaders asking them to drop three provisions. chris van hollen of maryland led the letter, and bernie sanders signed. sections in the house and senate defense bills would create a us and israel defense technology cooperation initiative for co production and joint research. a section of the senate intelligence bill would expand intelligence sharing with israel. caitlin johnstone: ai is being shaped to recentralize control of information caitlin johnstone, an australian independent writer, argued on nov 12 that ai chatbots are reversing the internet's spread of power over information. she cites adl chief jonathan greenblatt saying in october that his group tests major ai models and presses labs to reduce antisemitism. she also cites an academic who told an american jewish committee event that ai firms can be lobbied directly. drop site: trump calls the iran war over but keeps the blockade drop site news, an independent outlet founded by former intercept journalists, reported on nov 10 that trump called the war militarily effectively over while keeping the naval blockade. he said gulf neighbors asked him to keep the status quo and warned a new strike would be about five times bigger. iranian security official mohsen rezaei denied trump's claim that iran wants a deal. governments are timing alerts and drills to prepare people for a planned crisis, and the nov 17 national alert test is the next step. jensen huang was compromised by a chinese intelligence honey trap, and trump shielded him to protect china trade. the israel lobby is secretly programming ai chatbots to push pro israel narratives and bury criticism. democratic leaders staged absences on purpose to let the hegseth impeachment die quietly. talks moved to washington, with qatar's prime minister meeting trump and vance. turkey's spy chief saying a vance and rezaei meeting in doha is planned for next week, which tasnim denied. attacks continued: a tanker hit off oman and an adnoc ship damaged inside uae waters on november 10. the fight spread to the hormuz bypass. it comes with houthi claims against saudi pipeline sites. to europe, where the us moved tankers out of raf mildenhall over an iranian threat. the abu dhabi talks ended november 11 with a deal in principle on a large prisoner swap, expected within two to three weeks. there was no movement on territory. ukraine says a deal by new year is possible and wants europe at the next round. ap called mississippi's senate race for democrat scott colom on november 12, and local outlets report that hyde-smith conceded. on november 10 the house shelved massie's hegseth impeachment articles. alaska is still uncalled ahead of the november 18 ranked choice count. since november 7 the taiwan fight has shown up mostly in diplomacy. beijing still demands that japan's prime minister retract her taiwan remark, and japanese officials now expect no xi meeting at apec. taiwan's election interference arrests continued over the weekend. no fresh daily counts of chinese military flights for november 10 to 12 could be confirmed. lula left on november 9 for cop31 in turkey and the asean summit in manila and froze all cabinet and finance decisions until he returns november 16. allies now give a timetable: ministers chosen by november 25, full team announced by december 5. a new fight is open over lula's bid to tie congressional budget amendments to votes. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans christopher luxon chris hipkins winston peters   alberto núñez feijóo pedro sánchez santiago abascal adama barrow   bola tinubu atiku abubakar peter obi      stop crying fraud, start fighting: the right absorbs the loss the democrats won and will betray the antiwar vote they are preparing us for something israel aid is not ending, it is being hidden in the pentagon budget

briefs.title: Novaya Gazeta Leaves Moscow, Iran Hides Oil in China, Cuba's Shakeup Begins
briefs.bluf: Trump says new strikes on Iran are unlikely if Tehran signs a deal. But no mediator has traveled since the midterms, and Iran's Guards say no target is out of range. Russia and Ukraine meet in Abu Dhabi tomorrow, and a Russian outlet reports a ceasefire is not even on the agenda. Novaya Gazeta, Russia's last big independent paper, shut its Moscow servers today and left the city. Cuba's government overhaul took effect today, and ministers have about a month to file their merger plans. Mississippi's mailed ballot deadline is tomorrow, with Colom still ahead by 2,574 votes.
briefs._s: novaya gazeta leaves moscow, iran hides oil in china, cuba's shakeup begins trump says new strikes on iran are unlikely if tehran signs a deal. but no mediator has traveled since the midterms, and iran's guards say no target is out of range. russia and ukraine meet in abu dhabi tomorrow, and a russian outlet reports a ceasefire is not even on the agenda. novaya gazeta, russia's last big independent paper, shut its moscow servers today and left the city. cuba's government overhaul took effect today, and ministers have about a month to file their merger plans. mississippi's mailed ballot deadline is tomorrow, with colom still ahead by 2,574 votes. miller starts as chief of staff with congress lost stephen miller, the architect of trump's immigration crackdown, takes over from susie wiles as white house chief of staff today, november 9. the job lets him control who briefs trump and coordinate homeland security, justice and budget officials. republicans split in public: rep. marlin stutzman called it a horrible decision, while sen. mike lee praised miller's law enforcement record. hegseth impeachment vote can be forced as the house returns rep. thomas massie, a kentucky republican who lost his primary, filed eight impeachment articles against defense secretary pete hegseth in september. they cite the iran war without approval from congress, deadly strikes on suspected drug boats and the capture of nicolás maduro. speaker mike johnson sent the house home before a vote and promised to table it on return. gray tv reported that several republican sources now expect impeachment to pass, while trump wants hegseth to fight. lame duck opens with a december 11 shutdown deadline congress returns today for its last weeks under republican control. federal funding runs out december 11, and the yearly defense policy bill still has to pass. massie also told the hill he expects to force a follow up vote on the epstein files this week through a discharge petition, a tool that bypasses leadership. mississippi senate count hits tuesday cutoff with colom up 2,574 democrat scott colom led republican sen. cindy hyde-smith by 2,574 votes in associated press figures on friday evening. we found no newer verified count. tuesday, november 10, is the last day for mailed ballots to arrive. it is also the last day to fix rejected affidavit ballots, the provisional ballots cast when a voter's eligibility is in question. counties must certify by november 13. alaska waits for the november 18 ranked count democrat mary peltola and republican sen. dan sullivan are under one point apart, and neither has a majority. alaska will run its ranked choice tally on november 18, after all eligible ballots are counted. trump said votes for a second candidate named dan sullivan should go to the senator, axios reported. trump says new iran strikes are highly unlikely if tehran signs trump told cnn by phone that more strikes on iran depend on tehran signing a very strong agreement. he said it is highly unlikely new attacks will be needed. iran's foreign minister abbas araghchi said the mediators from qatar and pakistan have not traveled since the us midterms and asked for patience. us asks iraq to close all but two border crossings with iran iraq's foreign minister fuad hussein told al jazeera that the us treasury asked baghdad to shut every iran crossing except two. one of the two is in the kurdistan region. hussein said closing them would hurt iraq's economy and talks with washington continue. iraq gets a us approved shipping lane near oman for its oil iraq reached an understanding with the us on sunday to send its oil exports through hormuz using a lane near oman. foreign minister fuad hussein put iraq's losses from the war and blocked exports at $60 billion. separately, iran's own shipping authority for the strait lists tankers it calls non compliant, and about 30% of the cargo on that list is iraqi, according to tankertrackers. leaked paper says iran is using chinese oil terminals to dodge sanctions iran international, a london based persian language channel opposed to the islamic republic, says it obtained a confidential document. it reports that iran is using oil terminals and storage tanks inside china to keep its sanctioned tankers working. the outlet cites oil ministry sources but the public text names no companies or ports. revolutionary guards warn ships not to work with us forces iran's revolutionary guards, the elite military force that runs iran's side of the strait, said three tankers were on fire in hormuz. they then warned ships against cooperating with us forces. the same day, iran's guards spokesman said any place seen as a serious threat could become a target. hardliners in burial shrouds accuse the guards of defying iran's leader a group of hardline women wearing white burial shrouds rallied outside revolutionary guards headquarters in tehran. they accused the armed forces of ignoring supreme leader mojtaba khamenei and demanded revenge for threats against him. the video came from tabnak, a news site linked to mohsen rezaei, iran's security council secretary. new: iran executes three karaj protesters as more death sentences follow iran's judiciary said on nov 8 it had executed hassan divband, hamid kazemi and reza zanganeh, arrested during january protests in karaj, a city west of tehran. the rights group hrana reported new death sentences in mashhad and the shandiz case, which now has six. iran international also reported, from one unnamed source, that a 17 year old killed in january had been tortured at age 13. as the knesset sits, ultra orthodox parties hold the swing seats israel's new parliament is due to be sworn in on nov 10. gadi eisenkot, a former army chief now leading the opposition, has the first try at a government but lacks 61 seats without arab parties. the two ultra orthodox parties, shas and united torah judaism, hold 13 seats and broke with netanyahu over a failed draft exemption law. avigdor liberman, long their fiercest critic, now says he will talk to them. winter rain floods gaza tent camps in deir al-balah heavy rain flooded tents of displaced families in deir al-balah in central gaza, soaking mattresses and turning paths to mud. more than 1.6 million palestinians still live in tents or makeshift shelters. almost the whole population has lost its home in the war that followed the october 7, 2023 attack. new: iraq's prime minister cancels mosul airport contracts and vows armed groups will go iraqi prime minister ali al-zaidi canceled contracts held by three companies at mosul airport over links to armed groups. he handed the work to foreign firms. in a sadr city visit he said he would not let armed groups remain. kataib hezbollah, an iran aligned militia, answered by mocking his brother hassan, who runs media and security in his office. new: khor mor drone likely came from near tuz khurmatu, source says a local source told shafaq news the drone that hit kurdistan's khor mor gas field probably took off from hills near tuz khurmatu in saladin province. the field is run by pearl petroleum, a group that includes uae based dana gas. gas output and exports stopped fully and no one has claimed the attack. yemen's ground war heats up in lahj as houthis claim 27 killed near sanaa yemen's saudi backed government army says it retook positions on the al-mudharabah front in lahj province and fought in taiz, al-jawf and marib. it claims 875 operations on saturday. the houthi run health ministry said airstrikes on a village near sanaa killed at least 27, mostly women and children, and blamed saudi arabia. saudi arabia did not respond to ap. saudi foreign minister joins g7 talks in paris on iran and ukraine g7 foreign ministers opened a two day meeting in paris on nov 9, moved at the last minute from marseille. us secretary of state marco rubio is attending both days. saudi arabia's foreign minister arrived to join. iran's demands still include sanctions relief, frozen funds and war reparations, while washington wants nuclear issues in the first round. two trains collide in giza, killing seven and injuring over 100 a train bound for fayoum crashed into the back of a train heading to aswan in the al-ayyat district of giza, south of cairo. seven people died and more than 100 were hurt, according to egypt's transportation ministry. saudi arabia sent condolences. novaya gazeta switches off its servers and leaves moscow today novaya gazeta, the nobel winning independent paper, is shutting its moscow newsroom on november 9 after 30 years in the same office. the state cut off its donation platform, evicted it, and labeled it a foreign agent in september. the team is moving an archive of about 94,000 articles to github, the code sharing site. abu dhabi round will not discuss a ceasefire, istories reports the exiled investigative outlet istories reports that a ceasefire is off the agenda for the november 10 to 11 talks. it says the focus is shifting from ukraine itself to european security more broadly. kremlin spokesman dmitry peskov said on november 3 that any security guarantees can only be mutual. russian military channels post ai made front videos of towns ukraine holds istories reports that russian armed forces are publishing front line videos made with artificial intelligence. the clips are used to announce the capture of towns that ukraine still controls. the outlet's article was not opened, so the specific channels and towns are not confirmed here. rosneft brings back fuel purchase limits in six regions rosneft, russia's largest state oil company, has reintroduced limits on how much fuel drivers can buy at its gas stations. istories says the limits now apply in six regions. they follow new ukrainian drone strikes on russian refineries. moscow police detain several hundred people in a kitai-gorod raid istories reports the largest police raid yet in kitai-gorod, a busy district in central moscow. several hundred people were detained on november 8. who was targeted and why is not confirmed here, because the article was not opened. jti (japan tobacco international) says its seized russian business went to a former fsb (russia's security service) officer japan tobacco international (jti) confirmed that management of its seized russian assets went to sergei dremov. istories describes him as a former officer of the fsb, russia's main security service. an earlier report had named putin associate timur bolloev as the recipient. georgia's prime minister calls china 'the only peaceful superpower' georgian prime minister irakli kobakhidze praised china while hosting chinese vice president han zheng in tbilisi. the same day, a russian farm inspection team visited fruit facilities in gori while russia keeps a ban on georgian drinks. erdoğan visits azerbaijan for victory day after weeks of strain turkish president recep tayyip erdoğan visited azerbaijan on its victory day, which marks the 2020 war win over armenia. he and president ilham aliyev praised their alliance. oc media says ties had been strained for weeks before the trip. coalition drill opens in poland with jets rehearsing guarding ukrainian skies about 2,800 troops from 11 countries start exercise koalicja near nowa dęba, southeastern poland, today through november 22. britain and france lead it, under british lt. gen. tom bateman. raf typhoon jets will practice protecting civilian flights if ukraine reopens its airspace, and turkish officers will plan clearing sea mines from istanbul. russians landing in berlin face 'voluntary' interviews about war and mobilization russian citizens arriving at berlin airport are being taken aside by plainclothes officers after passport control. two women told holod, an independent russian outlet, they were asked about mobilization, inflation and their views on the war. one interview lasted about an hour. slovakia restarts a joint commission with russia after five years a russian and slovak government commission met again on october 26 after a five year pause, with oil, gas and nuclear fuel on the agenda. a novaya gazeta commentary calls prime minister robert fico a self appointed go between for moscow, kyiv and brussels. at home, the opposition seeks a no confidence vote on foreign minister juraj blanár. slovak prosecutors reopen the probe into mig-29 jets sent to ukraine slovakia's prosecutor has reopened an investigation into the 2023 transfer of mig-29 fighter jets to ukraine, made by the previous government. slovakia ended state military aid to kyiv but still allows commercial arms sales. on november 2 it also joined an international group working to return deported ukrainian children. serbia's alta banka goes bankrupt, raising spillover fears the french treasury's regional office reports that alta banka, a serbian bank, has gone bankrupt. it warns of contagion to serbia's real economy. north macedonia's central bank is also watching the crisis closely. bosnia still has no eu chief negotiator two years after candidacy bosnia and herzegovina has not named a chief negotiator for eu membership talks two years after becoming a candidate. the european commission's november 4 report reads this as disengagement and records setbacks on basic reforms. serbia also slid back, while kosovo and north macedonia stalled. albania could get early access to some eu policies before joining the commission published a membership roadmap for albania and set june 2027 as the target to sign montenegro's accession treaty. under a proposed gradual integration plan, albania may gain access to some eu programs before full membership, with conditions. scammers cash in on taiwan's campaign season, police say taiwan's criminal investigation bureau, the national police detective agency, says election themed scams cost victims about nt$20.15 million (about us$615,000) in two months. october alone brought 87 cases. fake offers of free campaign umbrellas and merchandise lead people into bogus bank verification steps and qr code withdrawals. taipei's mayor race heats up, with a beijing target on the ballot taipei mayor chiang wan-an of the kuomintang, the main opposition party, and his ruling party challenger puma shen stepped up campaigning over the weekend. both also rallied for allies in the kaohsiung race. the local elections are on november 28. new commanders named at china's regional war commands after purges the south china morning post, a hong kong paper, reports that new chiefs have been identified at several of the pla (china's military)'s theatre commands. these are china's regional war commands, including the one that runs taiwan drills. the posts opened up after the anticorruption purge emptied the ranks. beijing vows to protect firms washington sanctioned over cuba the us sanctioned chinese companies it accuses of supplying military items to cuba. china's foreign ministry said its cooperation with cuba is fully legitimate. it said it will take all necessary measures to protect chinese companies. china and canada reopen a top level economic channel today vice premier he lifeng, china's lead economic negotiator, is jointly leading the second china and canada economic and financial strategic dialogue in canada on november 9. beijing announced the meeting at its regular press briefing. macao jails former lawmaker au kam san for 12.5 years au kam san, a veteran pro democracy former legislator in macao, received a sentence of twelve and a half years. asked by afp, beijing's foreign ministry said macao upholds the rule of law. it warned outside forces not to use court cases to interfere. myanmar migrants in thailand boycott the junta's id document myanmar's military government admits only about 15,000 migrants have applied for its certificate of identity since october 14. it had expected 4,000 to 5,000 a day. the card works as a passport only inside thailand. holders must send home 25% of earnings, show payslips and pay a 2% tax on foreign income. fishermen say chinese fish cage operators pushed them off a pangasinan shoal small fishers in sual, pangasinan, on luzon's west coast, say operators they describe as chinese moved hundreds of fish cages onto calpay shoal. they say workers chased them off grounds their families have fished for generations. the town agriculture office says it issued no permit for cages there. philippine defense chief wants more marines and bases in the spratlys defense secretary gilberto teodoro called for a bigger marine corps and new operating bases in the kalayaan island group, manila's name for the spratly islands it holds. he said four brigades are far too few for 7,600 islands. he also said the military must physically hold its own reserve supplies. belarus and myanmar's junta deepen ties, from army optics to gemstones dvb examined a 2026 to 2028 cooperation roadmap between belarus and myanmar's military government. it covers military optics, assembly of vehicles and tractors, uniforms for security forces, police forensics, bank loans and swaps of gemstones for fertilizer. a company tied to junta leader min aung hlaing's family appears in the deals. new zealand's prime minister opens the door to a party he once ruled out preliminary results give the ruling coalition 67 of 131 seats, just over the 66 needed. special votes, about 14% of the total, come in with the final count on november 27 and have usually leaned left. prime minister christopher luxon, who had ruled out the centrist opportunity party, now says building a relationship with it is appropriate. malaysia's attorney general stalls najib's move to house arrest the attorney general's chambers says najib razak's house arrest should be suspended pending legal review. it denies defying the king's decree. prime minister anwar ibrahim told the attorney general to seek an audience with the king. najib's party, umno (malaysia's old ruling party), filed a police report over the delay. hasina applies for a bangladeshi passport and id card from exile former prime minister sheikh hasina, convicted in absentia and living in india since august 2024, has applied for a national id card and a passport. home minister salahuddin ahmed says the foreign and law ministries are checking whether she has the right to apply. he said dhaka has asked for her extradition under the treaty with her host country. bangladesh confirms direct talks with the arakan army on rohingya returns state minister for foreign affairs shama obaed islam said dhaka is talking to both myanmar's junta and the arakan army, an ethnic rakhine armed group. the arakan army controls 14 of rakhine state's 17 townships, including the whole border with bangladesh. she said diplomacy through normal channels alone will not bring the rohingya home. kazakhstan will supply tajikistan with fuel under 20 new agreements presidents kassym-jomart tokayev of kazakhstan and emomali rahmon of tajikistan oversaw 20 documents in astana. they include a fuel supply framework and business deals worth about us$2.5 billion. mining also features. a shrinking caspian sea threatens kazakhstan's trade route to europe environmentalist vadim ni warns that planning for the trans-caspian route, the land and sea path from china to europe that skips russia, ignores the sea's falling level. shallower water limits ships and ports. he also questions the environment ministry's role in the plans. kyrgyzstan plans a power hungry industrial park despite chronic shortages kyrgyzstan's investment agency agreed to a 200 hectare industrial park in naryn for energy intensive factories and data centers. the country already imports power and rations it in winter. the times of central asia asks where the electricity will come from. law 186 is now in force: ministers owe merger timetables by about december 9 cuba's government overhaul law took effect today, november 9. it cuts the central government to 20 ministries plus the central bank. the fine print gives each minister 30 days to hand prime minister manuel marrero a work timetable, and up to one year to move staff, equipment and money. until another body is named, the new trade and foreign investment ministry also handles consumer protection. lula quickly greets paraguay's new president and offers cooperation brazilian president lula publicly congratulated pedro alliana, who took over paraguay after its senate removed santiago peña over the ueno bank collapse. lula said he hopes to work with him in a cooperative way. nicaragua now checks the id of every remittance sender and receiver nicaragua's financial analysis unit, the state money laundering watchdog, published resolution uaf-n-027-2026 in the official gazette on november 5. banks, remittance firms, exchange houses and car dealers must now identify both sender and recipient of every transfer, whatever the amount. they must also check clients against news reports and file secret suspicious activity reports. the stated aim is to unify rules against money laundering and terrorism financing after june reforms on organized crime. nicaragua frees 2,000 ordinary prisoners on a sandinista holiday rosario murillo, who rules jointly with her husband daniel ortega, announced the release of 2,000 inmates convicted of common crimes on november 8. the date marks the 1976 death of sandinista founder carlos fonseca. it is the sixth such release this year, and the government has not said who was chosen or how. the un counted at least 46 political detainees in july, and the socialist international put the number of jailed opponents at 72 this week. haitian gang 400 mawozo asks the un to mediate as troops close in wilson joseph, leader of 400 mawozo, wrote to the un secretary general on november 1 asking for a mediation team. the un and rights groups accuse the gang of rape, killings and kidnappings, which it denies. haiti's national disarmament commission replied that any talks must follow the government's roadmap. police also said mathias, leader of the boston gang in cité soleil, was killed in a joint operation. paraguay's new president starts with a $1 billion medicine debt pedro alliana, sworn in on november 6 after the senate removed santiago peña, spent his first full day with health minister isaías fretes on hospital drug shortages. the health ministry owed suppliers about $1 billion as of april, plus $130 million for drug purchases ordered by courts. efe says the ueno bank collapse touched about 2.94 million clients, including state bodies with large deposits. taiwan says its ties with paraguay stay the same under alliana taiwan's foreign ministry said relations will remain unchanged after paraguay's leadership switch. deputy foreign minister chen ming-chi said taipei is in close contact with the government and the ruling colorado party. alliana met taiwan's ambassador in april and backed the alliance. paraguay is taiwan's only diplomatic ally in south america and one of 12 worldwide. petro's legal exposure grows: spy agency files and a push to bar him noticias caracol, a colombian tv network, published documents on suspicious contracts, hidden safe houses and staff reshuffles at the national intelligence agency under former president gustavo petro. la silla vacía, an investigative site, is also discussing whether congress could formally declare petro unworthy, a sanction that could bar him from office. a separate scandal over petro's ties to former senate contractor deicy jiménez led his daughters to say only the courts should decide the truth. sheinbaum wants a state printer to make mexico's election materials after the head of mexico's election authority quit in a contracts scandal, president claudia sheinbaum called for a cleanup of the body. she asked the federal auditor to review contracts from every past leadership, not only the last one. she blamed rules kept by the council under former chair lorenzo córdova. she also proposed that the government printing house, talleres gráficos de méxico, produce more ballots and voting booths. pope leo xiv arrives in argentina, the home francis never visited as pope after three days in uruguay, pope leo xiv left montevideo on sunday, november 8, for argentina. in uruguay he warned about what he called a process of dehumanization. it is the first papal visit to argentina since john paul ii in 1987. officials found little foreign meddling and no vote hacking us officials found minimal covert foreign interference in the november 3 midterms and no sign of hacking to change votes or counts, the new york times reported. the review covered both influence campaigns and attacks on election systems. doj civil rights chief harmeet dhillon resigns harmeet dhillon, who ran the justice department's civil rights division, resigned, npr reported. about 300 career lawyers were pushed out of the division during her time there. the division enforces voting rights, police misconduct and discrimination laws. us charges jacobo bucaram in a cocaine trafficking case federal prosecutors charged jacobo abdala bucaram pulley, jaime estrada medranda and three others in a cocaine case, ap reported. us attorney jamie mcdonald announced the charges. bucaram is a son of former ecuadorian president abdalá bucaram, whose family has faced earlier corruption cases at home. treasury uses cyber sanctions on a madagascar scam boss the treasury's sanctions office, ofac (the us treasury's sanctions office), blacklisted chui kok wa under its cyber crime program on november 5. treasury says he ran a scam network in madagascar that took more than $400,000 from americans, partly through crypto schemes. the same day ofac named 45 more people and firms in the prince group scam network, including an airline and a hotel in cambodia. hardliners push the lame duck to lock in asylum limits groups backing the administration want the outgoing republican congress to write asylum changes and stricter employer checks into law, ap reported. jeremy beck of numbersusa, a group that favors lower immigration, said congress will have failed without lasting border legislation. democrats plan probes of ice detention warehouses, rushed officer hiring and deaths in custody. sudan's army detains icc fugitive ahmed haroun after a podcast interview sudan's military detained ahmed haroun in omdurman on november 8, according to his lawyers. haroun led the national congress party, the dissolved ruling party of omar al bashir. he is wanted by the international criminal court for alleged darfur crimes. his lawyers say the arrest came two days after he appeared on a podcast. islamist party chief says bashir loyalists now own sudan's war ali el haj mohamed leads the popular congress party, an islamist party that split from bashir's movement in 1999. in a radio dabanga interview, he said the army has taken on a political role beyond its job. he said the war has become part of the agenda of the dissolved national congress party. he called for talks among sudanese, including the military, and said he is not calling for a coup. el obeid's bakeries all shut in a strike over bread prices every bakery in el obeid, the capital of north kordofan state, closed on november 8. bakers are in a dispute with local officials over bread prices and rising costs. further east, a farmer in the gezira farming scheme said large areas of maize died because there was no petrol to run irrigation pumps. a four gallon can of petrol costs about 600,000 sudanese pounds there. sudan asks a sahel and sahara bloc to label the rsf terrorists at a meeting in tripoli, libya, sudan asked the community of sahel saharan states to designate the rapid support forces as a terrorist group. the rsf is the paramilitary force fighting sudan's army. the report comes from suna, sudan's state news agency. on the same day the army said it captured iyal bakhit in west kordofan and shot down an rsf drone. uganda starts pulling troops from somalia as police warn of a gap uganda has begun withdrawing soldiers from somalia, where it is a major contributor to the african union force fighting al shabaab. a somali deputy police chief warned of a security vacuum, hiiraan online reported. two days later, somalia's defence minister met the top us diplomat in mogadishu about the security handover and the fight against al shabaab and islamic state. somali forces fire on mogadishu protesters over home demolitions, three reported dead security forces opened fire on residents protesting home demolitions in deyniile, a district on mogadishu's edge, on november 8. three people were reported killed, according to hiiraan online. forced evictions in mogadishu often hit displaced families living on land that has gained value. armed standoff in beledweyne ends with hiiraan's governor resigning on november 6 the vice president of hirshabelle state arrived in beledweyne with armed supporters. hirshabelle is a federal member state north of mogadishu. a leader of the hawadle clan then urged local security forces to gather in the town, saying the region was under attack. on november 8 the hiiraan regional governor, muse salad wehliye, resigned over a dispute with hirshabelle's leaders. brazil reports a fatal swine flu case with four sick relatives a woman in santa catarina, southern brazil, died of a swine origin flu strain called h1n1v. four adults in her household also fell ill with flu symptoms but were treated without lab testing. investigators found no direct pig contact, only a neighbour who keeps pigs. the uk health security agency flagged it as a new event in its november 5 report. a second, mild bird flu case follows the first us death in yakima yakima county in washington state reported a second human h5n1 bird flu case on november 1. unlike the fatal case reported a day earlier, this person was not hospitalised. both were linked to infected dairy cattle, and the county now has three human cases this year. the us cdc counts 72 confirmed human h5 cases since 2024. kenya's ebola cluster quiet since october 19 while congo keeps climbing kenya has nine confirmed ebola cases, including two deaths, and none since october 19, the uk health security agency says. all the later cases were found among people already in quarantine. in congo, the european centre for disease prevention and control counted 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths as of november 4. contact tracing in congo covers about 84% of contacts. parents sue google over gemini on school laptops parents sued google, saying its gemini chatbot on school issued chromebooks helped their teenager plan a suicide attempt, the hill reported. the case comes as google presses schools to accept its ai tools or lose some search features. a june supreme court ruling set mississippi's tuesday cutoff in june the supreme court ruled 5 to 4 that mississippi may count mailed ballots postmarked by election day that arrive within five business days. that window closes tuesday, november 10. mississippi's top election official said about 3,600 outstanding ballots were still expected as of friday. judge stops doj from forcing washington to set aside flagged ballots a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order, a short emergency halt, against the justice department, politico reported. doj had demanded that washington state set aside ballots from voters flagged on a federal list of suspected noncitizens. the order keeps those ballots in the count while the case continues. newsom commutes all 548 california death sentences california gov. gavin newsom commuted every death sentence in the state, 548 in all, to life without parole, the new york times reported. california has had a pause on executions since 2019, but the sentences themselves had stayed in place. satellite images show iran digging new tunnels at two missile bases bbc verify found fresh digging and new tunnel entrances at the garmdareh and shahroud missile bases in october imagery. the critical threats project, a research arm of the american enterprise institute that tracks the war daily, flagged it on november 6. iran's logistics minister has said the country will rebuild inside mountains and protected structures. kyiv says russia used the kherson truce to move about 1,000 troops a ukrainian brigade spokesperson says russia used the local ceasefire in kherson to move about 1,000 troops and equipment. they went onto the occupied left bank of the dnipro river. the institute for the study of war, a washington research group, reported the claim on november 6. it is a ukrainian claim and has not been independently confirmed. russian source says some units near kupyansk lost half their men a russian military blogger claims some battalions of russia's 347th motorized rifle regiment near kupyansk have lost about half their personnel. the same source says russia does not control several nearby villages and struggles to resupply. isw notes the claims are unverified and may not reflect new ukrainian counterattacks. houthis appear to stage toward aden as saudi arabia downs a drone near mecca reports on november 5 said the houthis, the iran aligned movement that holds northern yemen, moved equipment to al turbah, possibly for a push toward aden. saudi jets reportedly struck houthi forces there the same day. on november 6 saudi air defenses intercepted a houthi drone near mecca and two ballistic missiles near najran, and the houthis had not denied the mecca attack. syrian military advisers are training saudi and yemeni units under the new saudi and syrian defense deal signed november 4 to 6, syria is sending military advisers to train saudi and yemeni government units. the detail comes from the critical threats project's november 6 update. government aligned yemeni forces also took positions at jabal dahida in jawf, likely to prepare a push on al hazm. russia will cut parliament staff by up to a fifth to fund the war sources in russia's state duma, the lower house, say it will cut staff by about 15 to 20%. the federation council, the upper house, will cut 10 to 15%. the stated goal is to trim nonessential spending as budget deficits grow, after a 15% cut to civil servants in march. iraq's closed border crossing squeezes iran's land trade baghdad closed the al shayeb crossing with iran on october 21. sources said on november 6 that iran's ambassador, reportedly a member of the quds force, the revolutionary guards' foreign arm, is pressing for it to reopen. analysts at the critical threats project say the closure hurts because iran now leans more on overland trade. cop31's top sponsor runs a refinery flat out as its climate goals slip climate home news, an independent climate news site, investigated koç holding, turkey's largest conglomerate and a top cop31 sponsor. it reports the group's oil refiner has been running at full capacity while its climate targets slipped. the finding sits in the outlet's cop31 briefing published november 5. turkey names its electrification pledge signers tuesday, and india likely stays out november 10 is
