energy day at cop31, when turkey plans to launch a pledge to get 35% of final energy from electricity by 2035. today the figure is about 23 to 24%, and current policies reach only about 28%. australia has signed and europe likely will, but india is probably a no and china is undecided. cop31 opens with a fight over putting trade on the agenda the un climate summit opens today in antalya and runs to november 20. african countries want new agenda items on trade and adaptation money. china wants talks on trade rules that block clean technology exports, and european countries are expected to resist. even tripled, adaptation money would cover about a third of the need rich countries refused in bonn to write a target of tripling adaptation finance by 2035 into the text. a un report finds tripling would bring $85 to 120 billion a year against about $305 billion in needs. the list of indicators to track adaptation was also cut from 100 to 59 at the last minute. big emitters set to resist stronger cut language as china and india skip the leaders' days countries must decide whether the forum on cutting emissions continues, and in what form. saudi arabia, russia, india and china are expected to resist stronger wording. the leaders' segment runs november 11 and 12, and india and china are not sending top leaders. turkey warns cop31 visitors not to meddle in its internal affairs attendees were warned not to interfere in turkey's internal affairs, according to climate home news. government approval for a planned protest was still pending before the summit. turkey has faced criticism for its crackdown on civil liberties. state economists see $45.8 billion in local losses from amendment 3 florida's official revenue forecasters project local governments lose $4.95 billion in the first year, rising to $11.86 billion by 2031 to 2032, wgcu reported. that adds up to $45.8 billion over five years. neighbors are already counting: sarasota county faces $241 million over two years and manatee's sheriff more than $50 million. desantis wants the special session to block local workarounds gov. ron desantis said he will call a special session within two months, before his term ends in january, to put amendment 3 into effect. he wants to stop local governments from making up the loss by taxing residents in other ways, the news service of florida reported. school taxes are left out of the bigger homestead exemption. ben norton: voters rejected the iran war, democratic leaders still won't ben norton runs geopolitical economy report, a left wing outlet critical of us foreign policy. he argues the iran war reached voters through gas and grocery prices. he says senate democratic leader chuck schumer and house democratic leader hakeem jeffries remain pro war and pro israel. prashad: the sudan, yemen and iran wars are feeding each other vijay prashad directs tricontinental, a left wing research institute. he argues the wars around the red sea share foreign backers, port rivalries and smuggling routes. he says sudanese fighters sent to yemen after 2015 helped build the rapid support forces (rsf), the paramilitary now fighting sudan's army. real news network says a 2025 trump memo is jailing protesters for life the real news network is a left wing nonprofit video outlet. reporter ryan johnson says left wing protesters face life sentences under domestic terrorism charges. the piece ties this to a september 2025 presidential memorandum telling federal agencies to counter domestic terrorism. hartung and cortright: democrats won a mandate for peace william hartung is an arms trade analyst at the quincy institute, a think tank favoring military restraint. he and peace scholar david cortright read the midterms as a vote against war. they set out four priorities for the new congress, led by ending foreign wars and domestic repression. tucker carlson declares the end of the trump era tucker carlson is a former fox news host who now runs his own network. in his midterm episode he called the losses deserved. he blamed the iran war, living costs and israel policy, and said fox news hosts lobbied trump into the war. vaccine skeptic outlets fuse medical examiner emails with a bmj probe of fda naturalnews, a long running alternative health site, merged two stories. one is the defender's medical examiner emails. the other is a bmj investigation saying the food and drug administration's (fda) vaccine safety alarm could not see mrna harms. under israeli pressure, trump will use a nuclear weapon on iran's buried enrichment site during the lame duck period. federal health officials knew their safety system could not detect mrna vaccine harms and hid it, while medical examiners privately doubted safety. democratic senate candidates james talarico, sherrod brown and troy jackson abused students or staff, as shown in local tv reports. the november 17 national emergency alert test is the starting signal for the planned crisis governments are preparing people for. trump said on nov 8 that new strikes are highly unlikely if iran signs a strong deal, but araghchi says mediators have not traveled since the midterms. the blockade is spreading to land, with the us asking iraq to shut most iran crossings, while iraq won a us approved oil lane near oman. the guards warned ships not to cooperate with us forces. istories reports a ceasefire is not on the abu dhabi agenda and the focus is moving to european security. zakharova said on nov 7 the coalition drill proves europe has no place at the table. the drill starts today, and rosneft has brought back fuel limits in six regions after refinery strikes. stephen miller formally starts as chief of staff today as congress returns with a december 11 funding deadline and massie's pending hegseth impeachment resolution. mississippi's last day for mailed ballots and affidavit fixes is tuesday, november 10, with colom up 2,574 in the latest verified ap count. alaska's ranked choice tally is set for november 18. police put election season scam losses at about nt$20 million in two months, and the taipei mayor race between chiang wan-an and puma shen intensified. new chiefs were identified at china's regional war commands after the purge, and beijing kept pressing tokyo to retract prime minister takaichi's taiwan remarks. law 186 took effect today, november 9. no list of new ministers or job cuts was found on day one. the next hard date is about december 9, when ministers must give the prime minister their merger timetables. no new hoax threat or fridge hack attribution found in the window. germany's response to earlier sabotage is now visible: russians arriving in berlin are being questioned by plainclothes officers about the war and mobilization. no confirmed new development found in the november 7 to 9 window. unverified leads suggest lula is prioritizing a constitutional amendment negotiation and will not name ministers this week. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans christopher luxon chris hipkins winston peters   alberto núñez feijóo pedro sánchez santiago abascal adama barrow   bola tinubu atiku abubakar peter obi     the midterms were a referendum against the iran war and us backing for israel. governments are quietly telling people to prepare for a long emergency. altered local news clips briefs.title: Sunday Deep Dive: Eisenkot Gets the Mandate, a Leaked Russian Death Toll, and Iraq's Lights Go Out
briefs.bluf: The week's real shift was political, not military: US voters punished the Iran war, oil fell about 13% as traders priced in pressure for a deal, and on November 8 Trump told CNN new strikes are highly unlikely if Iran signs a strong agreement, even as minor US strikes continued. In Israel, Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate three days early, but his road to a government runs through Avigdor Lieberman's veto on the Arab parties, which now hold a record 19 seats. Russia and Ukraine meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11 with heavier delegations on both sides, as hackers released what they say are Rosstat records showing up to 450,000 Russian war deaths. Below the headlines: a drone strike shut Kurdistan's Khor Mor gas field as winter starts, Paraguay's bank collapse froze about $380 million of pension money, and Taiwan detained a pro Beijing party founder three weeks before its local elections. Mississippi's Senate race is still uncalled, with Colom ahead by 2,574 votes per AP.
briefs._s: sunday deep dive: eisenkot gets the mandate, a leaked russian death toll, and iraq's lights go out the week's real shift was political, not military: us voters punished the iran war, oil fell about 13% as traders priced in pressure for a deal, and on november 8 trump told cnn new strikes are highly unlikely if iran signs a strong agreement, even as minor us strikes continued. in israel, herzog handed gadi eisenkot the mandate three days early, but his road to a government runs through avigdor lieberman's veto on the arab parties, which now hold a record 19 seats. russia and ukraine meet in abu dhabi on november 10 to 11 with heavier delegations on both sides, as hackers released what they say are rosstat records showing up to 450,000 russian war deaths. below the headlines: a drone strike shut kurdistan's khor mor gas field as winter starts, paraguay's bank collapse froze about $380 million of pension money, and taiwan detained a pro beijing party founder three weeks before its local elections. mississippi's senate race is still uncalled, with colom ahead by 2,574 votes per ap. house democrats move toward impeaching hegseth as a fired admiral flips nancy mace's seat yahoo news' running midterm coverage on november 8 reported the house could vote this week on impeaching defense secretary pete hegseth, and that a navy admiral hegseth had fired won nancy mace's former south carolina house seat. details of the articles of impeachment were not collected this run. mississippi's affidavit ballot pileup traces back to a state roll cleanup that used experian credit data scripps reported that thousands of mississippians who showed up on november 3 found themselves marked inactive and had to cast affidavit (provisional) ballots, the main reason the hyde-smith and colom race is still uncounted. the state had used experian consumer address data to maintain its voter rolls; one voter said a clerk told him experian placed him in another city although he has not moved in a decade. experian says it has not served the state since 2025 and that its product supplied supplemental addresses and was never meant to validate voter records. the secretary of state's office did not answer scripps; npr separately reported that secretary michael watson's office could not say how many affidavit ballots remain, with over 9,000 processed by midday november 6. hyde-smith asks all 82 mississippi counties to set aside affidavit ballots; colom calls it unlawful hyde-smith's legal team wrote every county election commission asking that affidavit ballots be kept apart and each one's handling documented, citing state law on post election ballot handling. state gop chairman mike hurst called it a standard preservation step in a close race. colom's lawyers replied that state law has no provision for segregating counted affidavit ballots and that the demand threatens ballot secrecy. as of saturday afternoon ap had colom ahead by 2,574 votes, 49.1% to 48.8%, with about 97% counted; his lead has grown with each batch since election night. hyde-smith's campaign says thousands of votes remain in republican counties. alaska: a second 'dan sullivan' on the ballot drew about 3,600 votes in a race peltola leads by 637 with about a quarter of ballots still out, mary peltola led senator dan sullivan 48.02% to 47.72% as of november 4 afternoon, a 637 vote gap, with ranked choice tabulation starting november 18. a petersburg man also named dan j. sullivan drew roughly 3,600 votes. the sullivan campaign, citing a new york times report, says democratic operatives helped put him on the ballot and calls it the biggest cheating scandal in state history; the peltola campaign denies it. per just security's tracker, doj appealed the november 1 dismissal of its alaska certification suit to the ninth circuit the same day. incoming homeland security chair orders dhs to preserve every record as oversight democrats tell miller to 'lawyer up' representative bennie thompson, expected to chair house homeland security in january, wrote dhs secretary markwayne mullin demanding preservation of all records, emails and contracts. after trump named stephen miller chief of staff, representative robert garcia, the likely oversight chair, said democrats will keep investigating miller's conduct, with ice use of force, including the killings of alex pretti and renee good earlier this year, named as a top priority. hakeem jeffries said miller should be fired; mullin's public answer was that deportations will continue. free beacon: maine's new democratic senator troy jackson backed bills for clients of a firm where his son lobbied the washington free beacon reported that troy jackson's son chace joined a lobbying firm founded by jackson's former chief of staff in 2022, and that jackson, then a maine senate leader, introduced bills benefiting that firm's corporate clients, including one that would have let a lender avoid the state's interest rate caps. the son stopped lobbying when jackson left the state senate. the piece names neither the firm nor the bills and carries no response from jackson. hormuz traffic slowed but did not collapse under the october attack wave; old shadow fleet tankers are being pulled into legal gulf trades lloyd's list intelligence, the shipping data arm of the london trade paper, counted 116 non iranian cargo transits in the week of october 19 to 25, against 124 the week before, with the fall almost entirely in ships leaving the gulf while inbound traffic stayed near normal. ukmto, the british naval office that logs incidents, has recorded 144 events since the war began, and ships kept sailing in about three quarters of them. more than 50 tankers and gas carriers that were not under sanctions have shifted into gulf trades, and tonnage that once served iran, russia and venezuela is now being drawn into gulf exports. the brief is moving to a fortnightly schedule, next due november 19. russia agreed to give iran 90 helicopter mounted missile launchers, the financial times reports iran international, the london based persian language channel critical of tehran, relayed a financial times report that moscow agreed to supply 90 launchers for precision guided missiles that mount on helicopters. the same missiles are in wide use by russian forces in ukraine. neither the launcher model, the helicopter platform, delivery dates nor payment terms were given in the relayed text, and no iranian official response was reported. belgium's defense minister says tehran warned of 'dire consequences' if reza pahlavi spoke in brussels belgium's defense minister said on november 6 that iran warned his government of serious consequences if it allowed reza pahlavi, the exiled son of the last shah, to speak in brussels. the event went ahead. the minister also said the war between the us and iran affects belgian economic and security interests. iran international gave no detail on how the warning was delivered. tehran court sentences a social media activist to death over posts on x as executions pass 690 for the year a tehran court sentenced amirhossein mousavi, a social media activist, to death over his posts on x, according to his lawyer. separately, iran human rights, an oslo based monitor, counted at least 77 executions in october and 691 so far in 2026. these sit alongside the protester death sentences already reported from mashhad and isfahan. saudi led coalition says houthis tried to hit riyadh; the houthis now count 4,460 saudi strikes since the latest escalation on november 8 the coalition spokesman, turki al-maliki, said two ballistic missile launchers were destroyed in saada after an attempted houthi attack on riyadh, and that five missiles aimed at saudi territory were intercepted since dawn. houthi spokesman yahya saree claimed 91 saudi air and missile strikes in 24 hours across six provinces and a cumulative 4,460 since the latest round began. government forces claimed about 267 houthi fighters killed, wounded or fled on fronts from marib to taiz. nearly all figures come from the warring parties and are unverified. israeli press: an israeli strike on iran is still possible, but no major us buildup has been detected iran international relayed a ynet report, from israel's most read news site, that the israeli military is waiting on washington's next move and that a strike on iran remains an option. the same report said no significant new american military buildup had been seen. it came as trump weighed escalation against settlement after the midterm losses. herzog hands gadi eisenkot the mandate three days early; netanyahu answers with a 'national unity' pitch that keeps ben gvir president isaac herzog tasked gadi eisenkot, the former army chief who leads the centrist yashar party, with forming a government on sunday november 8, ahead of the november 11 deadline, after 67 of 120 lawmakers were not law enforcement officers in naacp v. blanche, judge reggie walton in washington ordered the government to file a status report by 7 a.m. on november 3 explaining how doj confirmed that none of its poll monitors that day were law enforcement officials. the report was filed and linked by the tracker, but its contents have not been summarized publicly. canadian extradited for allegedly hijacking university supercomputers in four states to mine crypto ryan james roach, 35, was extradited from canada and appeared in federal court in rochester, new york, accused with mathiew james stubbings, 41, of breaking into educational institutions' supercomputers in new york, tennessee, north carolina and massachusetts between 2016 and 2019 to run cryptomining software. stubbings is still fighting extradition in canadian courts. charges carry up to 10 years. treasury blacklists eight canadian money exchangers moving iranian funds through crypto, some tied to ryan wedding drug money on november 6 ofac designated eight canada based money services businesses in british columbia and ontario under executive order 13902, part of an irgc focused effort called operation economic outcast launched in august. treasury says they convert rials into digital assets, transacted with already sanctioned iranian exchanges such as nobitex and wallex and with irgc linked addresses, and changed names and addresses to evade detection; several also laundered proceeds for canadian trafficker ryan wedding. the action was coordinated with fincen, canada's fintrac and the dea, and the list entries include trx (tron) wallet addresses. new cuba sanctions reach two chinese state defense electronics firms supplying cuba's military a november 5 state department action under cuba executive order 14404 designated 8 entities, 2 individuals and 5 vessels. beyond the family members of gaesa leaders already reported, it hit china national electronic import and export company (ceiec) and beijing h&c technologies, a cetc international subsidiary, for contracting in 2026 with cuban arms buyer duna to supply components and surveillance equipment to cuba's armed forces. it also targeted the cyprus and panama owners and managers of cuban oil tankers (caroil, tentacool, petromarca, internacional maritima) and blocked the tankers esperanza, gloria c, maria cristina, emilia and lourdes. geo and corecivic post record ice revenue and say congress already funded detention through 2029 on november 5 earnings calls, geo group reported 2026 revenue up 14% to $2.2 billion and said it is selling its adelanto, california detention center to ice for close to $1 billion while continuing to run it; it is also opening three more centers. corecivic said revenue rose 27% to over $2 billion with four more centers activated, and its ceo lucibeth mayberry noted congress has funded ice through 2029. geo's ceo george zoley forecast another record quarter. federalist reads the exit polls the other way: immigration voters still broke republican the federalist's shawn fleetwood cites nbc and cnn exit polls showing 73% called immigration a crucial or major factor, with republicans winning that group 51% to 47% and the 36% who called it crucial 57% to 42%. the same polls showed 60% disapproving of how ice does its job. he warns republicans against any amnesty deal with the incoming democratic majorities. somalia after the ruling: a 30 day clock, a caretaker limit, and the ousted chief justice now says the president threatened him the supreme court ruling of november 5 did more than void the term extension. it set the end of parliament's mandate at april 14, 2026 and the president's at may 15, 2026, gave rival camps 30 days to agree an election framework and 90 days to vote, and confined the government to routine caretaker business until then. the court also rejected president hassan sheikh mohamud's november 4 dismissal of chief justice baashe yusuf ahmed, saying it bypassed the judicial service commission and parliament; the presidency says the firing answered complaints from judges, staff and lawyers, and maintains the march amendments give it until may 2027 to run one person, one vote elections. a garowe online headline dated november 8 reports the ousted chief justice accusing the president of threatening his security. nigeria: adc files appeal and stay against the ruling that voided atiku's nomination, tells inec to hold off a day after justice peter lifu of the federal high court in abuja declared the david mark led caretaker committee of the african democratic congress (adc, the main opposition coalition vehicle) illegal and voided the primary that produced atiku abubakar, the party filed a notice of appeal and a motion to stay execution. it formally notified inec, the electoral commission, and asked it not to take consequential steps while the appeal is pending. the suit was brought by nafiu bala gombe, a former deputy national chairman who argued he should have led the party after chairman ralph nwosu resigned. filing an appeal does not by itself suspend the judgment. australia sanctions both burhan and hemedti, an unusual move by a non traditional actor on sudan radio dabanga reports that australia on november 6 imposed sanctions and travel bans on four sudanese individuals, including army chief and transitional leader abdel fattah al burhan and rapid support forces (rsf) leader mohamed hamdan dagalo, known as hemedti, citing the war and human rights abuses. the listing treats both sides of the war symmetrically. the other two names were not given in the summary we saw. sudan's drone war shifts to the power grid: un counts 14 civilians killed and a four day hospital blackout on the white nile a un warning reported by radio dabanga on november 4 says drone strikes killed at least 14 civilians in el sunut, ed damazin, el zahour, khartoum and abyei, and that strikes on electricity infrastructure are causing widespread harm. in el dueim, white nile state, a four day blackout disrupted hospital services. in el obeid, the besieged capital of north kordofan, residents report fuel shortages and a lack of drinking water. earlier in the year a undp study put grid damage at about $3 billion. ethiopia: fano and tplf leaders appear together on video with the oromo liberation army, as tigray's interim government runs local polls that bar war veterans the critical threats ethiopia war security review (us think tank tracker) reports that on october 31 the 'alliance for survival' released a joint video of fano commander zemane kassie and tplf chairman debretsion gebremichael restating the aim of overthrowing the federal government, followed by a written statement with the oromo liberation army. federal forces reportedly entered sheraro on november 3 and claim to have captured tigrayan commanders including col. haile selassie assefa, described by one analyst as a liaison to eritrea, while fano reportedly took wuchale and ibnat. meanwhile the federally backed interim tigray administration began local elections in axum and abiy addi, with wazema radio reporting that veterans of the 2020 to 2022 war and party members are barred from running; civil servant salaries resume november 9. most battlefield claims are unverified. south africa's metros flip toward the da: about 40% in johannesburg, actionsa second in tshwane, mk holds ethekwini; final results due november 9 beyond the anc's collapse to about 32%, early metro counts reported by eyewitness news show the democratic alliance (da) at about 40% in johannesburg, 32% in tshwane, 30% in ekurhuleni, 45% in nelson mandela bay and 36% in mangaung, and above 60% in cape town, the only metro where it is projected to win outright. actionsa, herman mashaba's party, was at about 23% in tshwane, and jacob zuma's mk party led ethekwini (durban) at about 34%. ewn separately reported the country could face more than 100 hung councils. the electoral commission is expected to declare final results on sunday, november 9. us now bars anyone who was in congo in the past 21 days from boarding flights to the united states since 11:59 p.m. est on november 3, all international passengers to the us must attest they have not been in the democratic republic of congo in the previous 21 days, and anyone who has cannot board a commercial flight to the us, according to cdc guidance summarized by nature world news. us citizens arriving from uganda or south sudan are funneled through designated airports for enhanced screening. cdc says risk to the american public remains low. who's standing advice for this outbreak is against travel or trade restrictions. ebola reaches an eighth congolese province on the central african republic border; about 700 cases and 370 deaths added in nine days us cdc confirmed counts rose from 9,847 cases and 4,761 deaths on october 23 to 10,563 and 5,130 on november 1, with nord ubangi now among eight affected provinces; africa cdc counted 5,376 deaths as of november 2. kenya's cluster stands at nine cases and two deaths, all in nairobi and all linked to the first patient, with no community spread reported. nigeria's single imported case and a close contact were medically evacuated to switzerland on october 26, per ecdc. congo has begun testing whether ervebo, the licensed vaccine for the zaire strain, gives any cross protection against bundibugyo; no vaccine or treatment is approved for this strain. first us bird flu death of 2026: a yakima county dairy exposure as washington's cattle outbreak reaches 33 herds a yakima county, washington resident with underlying conditions died november 1 after severe avian influenza linked to infected dairy cattle, the first us death this year and the third since 2024. washington has reported three human cases since mid october, all tied to cows; a third case at a county dairy is mild. the h5n1 cattle outbreak has reached 33 herds in yakima county plus a dairy in benton county. health officer dave atteberry says public risk remains low, and contacts of the deceased are being monitored; no sequencing results have been released. democrats line up ai model testing, liability and an ai agency; one analyst says must pass bills are the route reuters reported representative lori trahan will push bills requiring independent experts to test leading ai models and clarifying company liability for harmful ai actions, representative greg casar wants ai executives to testify under oath, and senator elect abdul el-sayed has called for an independent ai agency. in october, zoe lofgren and other house democratic committee leaders asked openai, anthropic, meta, google and spacex to detail their security practices and report ai tools acting in unintended ways. raymond james analyst ed mills said legislation is likelier than markets assume, through riders on must pass bills or a veto override push. exit poll: 56% called ai and data centers a major factor; new senators want a moratorium and full energy cost recovery ssrs exit polling cited by the national news desk found 56% of voters called ai and data centers crucial or major to their vote. senator elect annie andrews of south carolina backs a two year data center moratorium, senator elect roy cooper of north carolina wants data centers to pay their full energy cost, and representative ted lieu promised public ai hearings. openai announced commitments on data center energy costs and jobs less than 48 hours after the election and called for clear rules. meta, tiktok and alphabet sue california over a law against 'psychologically exploitative' feeds for kids 15 and under the three companies filed coordinated but separate federal suits in san jose, san francisco and los angeles against ab 1709, signed by governor newsom in september, which bars platforms from deploying addictive design features for users 15 and younger. they argue it violates free speech, conflicts with section 230, and takes decisions that belong to parents. the law is set to take effect january 1. en banc ninth circuit rules private groups cannot sue under the voting rights act's voter intimidation clause in seiu v. department of justice, the full ninth circuit on november 3 reinstated a panel decision that section 11(b) of the voting rights act, which bars intimidating voters, gives private parties no right to sue, and denied rehearing the same day. on november 4 the district court in san francisco stayed the union's preliminary injunction bid while the government's appeal is pending. the case concerned doj election day activity in california. boasberg rejects dhs bid to punish plaintiffs over the voter list they obtained in discovery in trujillo and coalition for humane immigrant rights v. dhs, chief judge james boasberg in washington on november 3 denied the government's motion claiming plaintiffs violated a court order in handling a list of voters disclosed in discovery. the suit challenges dhs's effort to match voter rolls against immigration data to find suspected noncitizen voters. war on the rocks: killing iran's top leaders made tehran harder to deal with, not easier war on the rocks' members newsletter says that with the us midterms over, the us and iranian standoff is stuck and the next move belongs to washington. it lists a munitions shortage and a public that does not want renewed war as practical limits on a new campaign. a companion podcast with former cia analyst cole bucy argues iran's leadership changed in kind when supreme leader ali khamenei was killed on the war's first day in february, so tehran now gains little by playing it safe. kyiv's forecasts of 30,000 to 100,000 more north korean troops never materialized writing in the lowy institute's interpreter, boston college researcher khang vu tracks ukrainian warnings that rose from up to 100,000 extra north korean soldiers (november 2024) to 50,000 (august 2026); none arrived. he puts the current force at 14,000 to 16,000, about 9,500 of them active duty soldiers in artillery, rocket and drone roles around kursk. a north korean laborer reportedly earns about $7,500 a year versus about $24,000 for a soldier, and the arms trade with russia is valued at $14.4 billion. pakistan briefly barred taiwan's two big airlines from its airspace under the one china policy in october pakistan reportedly denied overflight to china airlines and eva air, taiwan's two main carriers; defence minister khawaja asif said only mainland china is allowed under the one china policy. the ban was quickly reversed and access restored until march 27, 2027, with no word on what happens after. beijing itself does not restrict taiwanese airlines this way. a former biden aide argues the midterm loss leaves trump's foreign policy hand largely intact cory alpert, a university of melbourne researcher who spent three years in the biden white house, argues democrats' gains repudiated tariffs and the iran war as cost of living issues, yet trump keeps unilateral foreign policy control until january 2029. democrats gain the budget process and investigative power, including probes of corporate executives with foreign government deals. foreign governments, he says, now have reason to hedge for two full years. war on the rocks names a new class of defense contractor: the 'neo primes' a november 2 essay by journalist sharon weinberger and analyst jonathan panter examines how technology companies are becoming major pentagon contractors alongside the traditional prime contractors. only the title and byline were checked; the full argument was not read. markets now price a december fed rate hike at about 77% as the bank of england raises to 4% after october payrolls beat forecasts by more than double and unemployment fell to 4.1%, futures put the odds of a federal reserve hike in december near 77%, up from 67% a day earlier, with one more hike priced for 2027. the bank of england raised its rate to 4.0% after six cuts last year. wage growth slowed to 3.1%, below forecast. bank of england reportedly questions lenders on loans to data centers with no tenant signed citing bloomberg, bullionvault reports the uk central bank is asking banks about lending to data center projects that have no tenant in place. the nasdaq 100 fell 6.5% on november 5, its steepest single day drop in more than 18 months, and sat 9% below its october 6 record; about $6 trillion was erased from equity markets in the week. bitcoin traded like a tech stock, not like gold, in the week's rout bitcoin fell more than 6% on november 5 to $75,463 on bitstamp, its lowest since september 16, briefly breaking its 50 week average. crypto liquidations neared $850 million in 24 hours, per coinglass. gold, by contrast, rose 4.1% for the week to about $4,050 an ounce. vietnam's other trade pacts could hand washington's concessions to its rivals law lecturer tran hoang tu linh notes vietnam signed a trade deal with efta (switzerland, norway, iceland, liechtenstein) on october 18 whose article 4.4 requires equal treatment for efta service suppliers. the cptpp pacific trade pact has similar clauses. if the pending us deal lets american investors exceed vietnam's 49% cap on foreign ownership in facilities based telecoms, japanese, australian or canadian investors could demand the same. oil fell about 13% on the week as traders priced a democratic congress as pressure for an iran deal brazil's jornal do comércio reports brent for january settled at $98.32 and wti for december at $90.83 on november 6, with futures down about 13% over the week. the paper attributes the slide to bets that the democratic win gives washington more reason to seek a diplomatic exit, while noting a peace deal remains distant amid continued gulf attacks. us gasoline hits its 2026 low at $4.10, but only a fraction of crude's drop reached the pump the aaa national average was $4.10 a gallon on november 5, down from $4.17 on november 2, yet still about 34% above the $3.06 thanksgiving 2025 average. only about 7 cents of a potential 18 to 24 cent decline had passed through. analyst tom kloza warned refined product prices may stay high well after crude eases. argentina takes the uk to the law of the sea tribunal over the falklands' sea lion oil field; hearings november 10 and 11 argentina has asked the international tribunal for the law of the sea in hamburg for provisional measures against the uk's approval of the sea lion offshore project, about 107 nautical miles north of the falklands (malvinas), licensed to navitas petroleum with rockhopper exploration. a full arbitral case would follow. international law professor donald rothwell says the tribunal cannot rule on sovereignty, which the claim depends on. silver up 6.3% from its 2026 low as copper slides; metals split on war and rate bets silver traded near $51.80 an ounce on november 6, up 6.3% from monday's low for the year, while copper fell 3.5% on the week. gold rose 4.1% from a 13 month closing low the previous friday. cop31 opens november 9 in antalya under an unusual split presidency the un climate summit runs november 9 to 20 in antalya: türkiye hosts and runs the voluntary action agenda, australia manages the formal negotiations, and türkiye insists it has the final say. türkiye will launch a pledge on november 10 for electricity to supply 35% of final energy by 2035, up from about 23 to 24% today. climate action tracker projects only about 28% under current policies. brazil publishes a 182 page voluntary fossil fuel roadmap with a 2033 timetable released november 3, brazil's roadmap for moving away from fossil fuels sets a timetable to 2033. european and small island states may try to reference it in the cop31 cover decision, while producer states oppose it. brazilian officials say it is not a formal document requiring negotiation. the ipcc still cannot agree when its next major reports are due, after a sixth failed attempt governments are split on whether the ipcc's seventh assessment reports (ar7) will be ready for the 2028 global stocktake, the five yearly review of the paris agreement. the panel's last meeting was suspended after a sixth failure to agree on a timeline. the question will come up at antalya. loss and damage fund holds $342 million against $2.8 billion in first requests a german green party foundation briefing says the un fund for climate loss and damage has a $342 million startup phase while initial requests total $2.8 billion. it also says adaptation finance was $31.7 billion in 2024, mostly loans, against an annual gap of about $387 billion. lowering global temperature by 0.1°c after overshoot would need about 200 billion tonnes of co2 removed, four to five years of global emissions. amendment 3 passed with about 62%; lee county's own staff projected $121 million then $159 million in cuts florida voters approved amendment 3 with roughly 62%, above the 60% threshold; it raises the homestead exemption on non school property taxes by $150,000 next year and $250,000 in 2028. in a september workshop lee county staff projected required cuts of $121 million in 2027 and 2028 and $159 million the following year, with public safety, animal services, parks and the 20/20 land buying program at risk. options laid out included new taxing units (mstus), higher user fees, bonds or a higher millage rate; commissioner cecil pendergrass noted residents may still pay through fees. separately, state general revenue came in $429 million above projections in september. desantis promises a property tax special session with a grant pool for rural sheriffs, and another citizens rate cut desantis said the legislature will set dates for a special session to implement amendment 3 by january 1, including a schedule of further homestead relief, limits on local governments raising revenue other ways to get around it, and a grant pool worth tens of millions for core needs such as rural sheriffs. school districts are excluded. he also announced another auto insurance rebate and said he expects citizens property insurance to cut rates again in south florida by year end or early next year. cape coral elects retired green beret rick erickson mayor by 2,840 votes rick erickson, 63, a 32 year army veteran, won about 52% against lisa cohen-adkinson, who said he won with distortions and personal attacks. he is set to be sworn in as the city's 17th mayor on november 18. incumbent john gunter, appointed in 2021 after mayor joe coviello's death, finished third of seven in the primary. patrick lawrence: aipac's exit from direct endorsements is a retreat into shell pacs, not a surrender in a consortium news column, patrick lawrence argues that aipac's october decision to stop endorsing candidates and giving directly moves its money into short lived and shell political action committees (pacs, groups that raise and spend campaign money) that hide donors. he points to the michigan senate primary, where abdul el-sayed beat mike rogers 52 to 48 after aipac aligned money backed haley stevens, and to a pending defense bill provision he calls ndaa section 219. jeffrey sachs: the midterms were a referendum on the iran war, so peace is now good politics economist jeffrey sachs argues voters punished the iran war and its costs and that democrats should run on an antiwar platform: reclaim war and spending powers, settle ukraine on neutrality terms, end support for israel's wars and cut the military budget. he cites the ap voter survey showing about 60% called the use of force against iran wrong and about 90% named cost of living a major factor, plus gasoline rising from about $2.80 to a $4.43 monthly average by september. providence voters pass a 75% divestment ordinance, making it the largest us city to divest from israel providence, rhode island voters approved question 7, a citizen initiated ordinance, with about 75% on november 3. it orders the city to divest from companies and countries profiting from genocide, apartheid or prolonged occupation, without naming israel; local activists say the city holds millions in israel bonds. the coalition gathered over 10,000 signatures after outgoing mayor brett smiley blocked a council version. moon of alabama predicts a lame duck trump may strike iran around the november 8 to 9 new moon the blogger known as 'b' at moon of alabama, a german run anti establishment site focused on war coverage, wrote that trump might renew strikes on iran around the new moon because the military prefers darkness. he says outright he does not know, and argues a weakened trump may want a dramatic legacy act while the democratic congressional leadership will not change policy much. moon of alabama: stephen miller's promotion protects defense secretary hegseth moon of alabama argues that naming stephen miller white house chief of staff shields pete hegseth from being made the scapegoat for the iran war and the midterm loss. the post leans on a new york times account of miller's role, hegseth's public congratulations and reporting on the two men's close social ties. georgia's secretary of state finds an uncounted memory card that flips a state house seat to the republican a routine check after the election found about 388 more voters checked in than ballots reported in seminole county, part of southwest georgia's house district 154. counting the missed election day memory card turned democrat harry james' 58 vote lead into a 262 vote lead for republican gerald greene. secretary of state brad raffensperger called the failure unacceptable and opened an investigation; zerohedge relayed the ajc, wctv and the current. city journal sting: an la immigrant rights group hosted an official voting center while staff recommended candidates christopher rufo and two colleagues report that chirla, a los angeles immigrant rights nonprofit that has received over $100 million in california funds since 2019, hosted an official county voting center during a get out the vote event where an employee walked them through which candidates to pick. they argue this may break california's 100 foot electioneering rule and federal limits on 501(c)(3) charities, and urge the irs and treasury to act. zerohedge republished the piece. kunstler on zerohedge: the midterms were a fraud built to launch a 'color revolution' novelist and blogger james howard kunstler claims democrats registered ineligible and fictitious voters to flood the count with mail ballots, then plan riots and a push to declare trump illegitimate, possibly leading to the insurrection act. he says a doj voter roll audit will expose it, and alleges minnesota fraud involving peggy flanagan and tim walz. epoch times: trump backs nvidia's jensen huang despite a probe into his affair with an alleged chinese spy the epoch times, a paper founded by falun gong followers and hostile to beijing, reports that nvidia's board opened a probe into whether ceo jensen huang was targeted by chinese intelligence after he admitted an affair with 'alice huang', an executive at megaspeed, a singapore firm that is a major nvidia customer. trump called huang honorable, said he had heard of no wrongdoing and floated bringing him on next week's china trip. rubio called it an internal corporate matter. war room: bannon says 'caravans' are already moving after the democratic win on war room, steve bannon's daily show on real america's voice, bannon said on november 4 that caravans were already heading north and that central americans believed the gates were open again, without sourcing. laura ingraham, brian kilmeade, the gateway pundit and alex jones' site carried versions the same week, according to media matters. former cia officer kiriakou: the agency told the white house three times that iran had no bomb program on judge andrew napolitano's libertarian show judging freedom, former cia officer john kiriakou said three separate national intelligence estimates before the war concluded iran had no nuclear weapons program, and that analysts judged the war a mistake. he also cited a leaked cia 'red cell' paper suggesting israel, not iran, could break apart. zerohedge carried the segment, which also featured former analyst larry johnson. the midterms were stolen by fraud, possibly through hacked tabulators, as the opening move of a democratic 'color revolution' (new hooks since nov 7: a michigan tabulator wifi claim and a real georgia memory card error) a new migrant caravan was organized and timed to the democratic midterm win, possibly funded by moneyed interests netanyahu planned a provocation or attack on iran to swing israel's election and drag the us back into war nvidia's jensen huang was compromised by a chinese intelligence honey trap, and trump is protecting him for the china trip the israel lobby is going underground, moving money into shell pacs to secretly split progressive votes no new confirmed tanker strike for november 7 to 8 surfaced in sources checked. the newest hard data (lloyd's list, november 5) shows traffic slowed rather than collapsed, with outbound gulf cargo the casualty, while israeli press says a strike option remains open pending washington. an ft report of russian helicopter missile launchers for iran adds a littoral capability relevant to the strait. delegations are now set: umerov leads kyiv's team with budanov, arakhamia and kyslytsia, while moscow added deputy foreign minister ryabkov and military officials under medinsky. france says europe will take part, the kremlin says it will not, and zakharova tied the coalition 26.2 drill starting november 9 to that dispute. hacker leaked rosstat data claiming up to 450,000 russian war deaths landed on november 8. mississippi is still uncalled: ap had colom ahead by 2,574 votes on saturday with about 97% counted, and hyde-smith has asked all 82 counties to set aside affidavit ballots. alaska's ranked choice tally is november 18. incoming democratic chairs answered stephen miller's promotion with investigation pledges and a dhs records preservation demand. election security cases are accelerating three weeks before the november 28 local vote: prosecutors detained the founder of the taiwan people's communist party over alleged ccp funding of ward chief races, a retired general in a separate beijing money case got bail, and the mac tallied 131 people targeted by transnational repression. militarily, three more f-16v block 70 jets arrived on november 8; no new large scale pla drill was found in the window. on november 6 the state movement's name; its founder denies involvement. no official attribution yet, and no new information found on the supermarket fridge hacks. lula held an unscheduled macroeconomic meeting at the alvorada on november 5 that included mantega, coutinho and heterodox economists alongside alckmin and durigan, while the finance choice remains open. no new court filing by flávio bolsonaro was found briefs.title: Paraguay Ousts Its President, Sudan Accuses Ethiopia, Iran Faces a Winter Gas Crisis
briefs.bluf: This edition was rebuilt around what most outlets missed. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña 44 to 0 after a bank collapse froze deposits for nearly half the country, putting one of Taiwan's last allies in flux. Sudan formally accused Ethiopia at the UN of hosting RSF drone launches, as Ethiopia's own war reignites on three fronts and an Ebola outbreak in Congo passes 10,700 cases with spread to Kenya and Nigeria. In the Gulf, Iran faces a winter gas shortfall and is executing protesters while it negotiates, the Houthis are licensing Red Sea shipping by email, and Gulf fertilizer and sulphur exports are down about 70%, a food and metals shock that will hit after the oil headlines fade. In Washington, Stephen Miller becomes chief of staff Monday and a judge threw out the DOJ suit against Alaska's Senate certification.

hanging after retracting his confession. iran human rights counts at least 36 protesters executed since march. gas rich iran faces a winter shortage and leans on russia the national gas company says about 130 million cubic meters a day, roughly 16% of last year's output, is still offline after the march strikes. about 11 provinces could face shortages. hardliners float leaving the nuclear treaty; putin saw the finnish and norwegian call as an opening to europe per farida rustamova's vlast newsletter, putin views finland and norway as softer than berlin, paris and london; both want a standing anti aircraft missile tests and a cruise missile dropping cluster munitions on a mock runway; nk news found the images heavily manipulated. border loudspeakers are installed but silent. pyongyang's quiet diplomatic thaw before apec kim jong un's international department chief went to beijing ten days after kim visited dandong; brazil's first ambassador in a decade took up his post. kim yo jong emergency rule in khyber pakhtunkhwa on october 11, former chief minister sohail afridi and two pti lawmakers are in 'protective custody' and 200 plus public order cases were filed. coalition partner energy, and this time did not blame the embargo. paraguay's senate removes president santiago peña, who is detained at home the senate voted 44 to 0 to remove peña for poor performance after the court and electoral council members by year end, declare the presidency vacant, then hold a vote within six months, possibly july 24. venezuela's reserves fall despite $90 oil oikos research finds venezuelan troops from its 2027 military permits but keeps russia decree 13/2026 lists foreign forces allowed in for exercises; for the first time since 2020 cuba and venezuela are out, russia keeps the largest quota. bukele's 2,000 troops in haiti operate outside the un force about 2,000 salvadoran soldiers with armor and air support deployed after an october ambush; the un says most sit outside the gang suppression force. a gang boss wrote to the un seeking a truce. colombia's forensic institute pushes back on soldiers moving bodies after combat medicina legal asked that troops be barred us troops, now held in louisiana; 66 democratic lawmakers asked rubio to cancel the flights, reportedly routed through pakistan. sudan takes ethiopia to the un security council over rsf drones mohamud's one year extension unlawful and that his term ended in may; he had dismissed chief justice bashe yusuf ahmed the night before. uganda will pull all its troops out at the end of next year. will appeal and blames the ruling apc, which denies a role. guinea expels more than 8,000 burkinabè gold miners expulsions followed a ban on artisanal mining in northeast guinea; burkina's security minister says miners were injured and killed and ouagadougou got no notice. tanzania acquits tundu lissu of treason but jails him four years for incitement the opposition leader, held 19 months, was cleared of the capital charge and convicted of a lesser one he was never charged with. bundibugyo ebola passes 10,700 confirmed cases, with spread to kenya and nigeria as of november 4, drc had 10,741 bunia october 23. guinea bissau cancels a us funded hepatitis b trial that withheld vaccine from newborns the study would have enrolled 14,000 newborns, half without the birth dose who recommends; barbara lagoa upheld an order requiring florida to explain the income and household figures it used to end coverage for nearly 500,000 people. fort myers ousts its mayor; lee school board chair loses city employee amber ware unseated mayor kevin anderson, and crystal johnson beat lee school board chair armor persons. florida's amendment 3 passed with about 62%; state economists project a $45.8 billion five year hit to local governments. vips memo: 'iran is not bluffing' veteran intelligence professionals for sanity, including ray mcgovern, larry johnson and scott ritter, tell trump iran briefs.title: Markets Turn on the AI Buildout, Iran Talks Stall on Sequencing, Two Senate Seats Still Open
briefs.bluf: The Iran war is still the defining factor. Three more tankers were damaged near Qatar on November 5, Trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while Qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and IAEA access for reopening Hormuz. Wall Street had its worst day in years: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since March 2020, on fears that a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats with Mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and Alaska (ranked choice tally November 18) still open, and a Justice Department suit over a second Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot is the main certification risk. In Cuba, Yoani Sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the Law 186 government overhaul takes effect November 9. Ukraine talks move to Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 after a White House event marking the Oleshky humanitarian truce.

futures point to a partial rebound this morning. democrats hold 54 senate seats with mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and alaska (ranked choice tally november 18) still open, and a justice department suit over a second dan sullivan on the alaska ballot is the main certification risk. in cuba, yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the law 186 government overhaul takes effect november 9. ukraine talks move to abu dhabi november 10 to 11 after a white house event marking the oleshky humanitarian truce. two senate races still open democrats hold 54 seats and flipped iowa, kansas, maine, ohio, north carolina, south carolina and texas. in mississippi, democrat scott colom leads sen. cindy hyde-smith 49.0% to 48.9% with about 3,600 mail ballots left; certification is due november 13. in alaska, mary peltola leads sen. dan sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% with ranked choice results due november 18. doj suit could stall alaska certification the justice department sued in october to block certification if peltola wins by less than the vote total of a second, unaffiliated candidate named daniel j. sullivan, arguing voters may have been confused. trump said he ordered the suit and has urged prosecuting peltola. legal scholars say the statute does not let doj enjoin a state certification. judge pauses the trump arch; la picks a new mayor a federal judge blocked construction of the planned arch for 14 days. in los angeles, nithya raman defeated mayor karen bass. in california, gov. newsom commuted 548 death sentences. more tankers hit; trump weighs a heavier strike the irgc said three more tankers were damaged november 5, two by mines and one by fire. ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump said he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but may have to, met his national security team, and spoke with the qatari emir, who urged restraint. a carrier group is heading to the region via singapore. diplomacy stuck on sequencing iran sent a nuclear proposal through qatar that it will discuss only after the us meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations. a qatari draft reported by axios has the us lift the blockade and release some frozen funds and iran invite the iaea to bombed sites on day one, with hormuz reopening on day two and nuclear talks on the enriched uranium stockpile after that. iranian sources told reuters another us attack is more likely than a deal. tehran leans on the region foreign minister araghchi called his counterparts in the uae, qatar, saudi arabia, turkey, pakistan, oman and egypt. parliament speaker qalibaf mocked vice president vance as a losing gambler after vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. israel: herzog weighs who forms the next government after the october 27 election left netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and gadi eisenkot's at 48, president herzog began consultations, meeting the smallest parties first. eisenkot was expected to have more endorsements than netanyahu. the election commission reviewed 9,069 polling stations and found no fraud. white house marks the oleshky truce melania trump hosted russian envoy kirill dmitriev and ukraine's david arakhamia to mark the six day humanitarian ceasefire in occupied oleshky (october 27 to november 1). more than 750 people were evacuated; russia refused to extend it. president trump met dmitriev but not the ukrainians and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks next week witkoff and kushner lead the us side at three way talks in abu dhabi november 10 to 11. german chancellor merz hosts a coalition of the willing summit november 19. russia holds about 80% of donetsk. yoani sánchez released; two journalists still held yoani sánchez, director of 14ymedio, was released after more than nine hours in custody. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet, arrested november 2, and henry constantín, jailed since september 16, remain detained. rsf, the inter american press association and amnesty international condemned the detentions. law 186 reshapes the government from november 9 the law, approved july 30 and published november 2 in the gaceta oficial, cuts the cabinet to 20 ministries plus the central bank and merges commerce, construction and agriculture into fewer bodies. officials present it as streamlining; critics see a shuffle that leaves the economic model untouched. protest count stays high the observatorio cubano de conflictos logged 542 protests and complaints in october and 85 repressive events. transition quiet no new annulment filings or street mobilization found. lula takes office january 1. pope leo begins south america tour the first us born pope is in uruguay november 6 to 8, argentina november 8 to 11 and peru november 11 to 17, about 50 events in 10 cities, including a return to chiclayo, where he was bishop, and a meeting with president milei. former fbi agent charged doj charged former fbi agent andrew reyes on november 5. details of the charges were not collected this cycle. election claims fade, alaska suit gives them a new hook rigging claims about the midterms have lost momentum as most losers conceded, but the doj suit over the second dan sullivan gives the "stolen seat" framing a new focus in alaska. fridge hacks: still no attribution no group has claimed or been named for the attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called them deliberate. the danfoss and copeland flaws were disclosed by claroty august 9; forescout counted about 13,000 exposed systems. the pentagon is reviewing august freezer failures at military commissaries. mexican judge arrested in ryan wedding case a mexican judge was arrested over an alleged $2 million bribe tied to the case against ryan wedding, the former olympic snowboarder accused of running a cocaine network and ordering the killing of a federal witness. wedding was captured in mexico in january. doj launches super intelligence task force the department announced a task force on ai related crime the same day it charged a $129 million fraud marketed as a super intelligence investment. no new ofac actions found for november context: the cartel del noreste was designated october 13, venezuela's jorge rodríguez was delisted october 14, and foreign banks must exit panama's bicsa by november 14. deportations deepen school enrollment drops npr reports ice enforcement is accelerating enrollment declines in districts with large immigrant populations. doj also sued penn state over in state tuition for undocumented students. why the doomsday date keeps spreading writers revisiting the 1960 "doomsday" paper note that a specific date, a real scientific source and a friday the 13th make a claim shareable. the historian alan maceachern argues the lesson is about how confidently findings are presented. ai selloff after the election nvidia fell 9.2%, about $440 billion in value, and the largest tech stocks lost more than $1 trillion as investors priced in a congress that may slow data center and chip spending. south korea's kospi fell about 8 to 9% and halted trading. google: accept ai or lose search in schools from early 2027, gemini and search will be off by default on k-12 student accounts; schools that switch ai off entirely will also lose search. fairplay urged schools to consider other search engines. supreme court hears labor visa case november 10 department of labor v. sun valley orchards is argued monday. claim: a scientist said the world ends november 13 the date comes from a real 1960 science paper. its authors fitted a curve to population history that reached infinity in late 2026, and they picked friday the 13th partly as a joke. population growth peaked soon after and the curve stopped matching reality. hundreds leave oleshky more than 750 civilians left the occupied town during the six day truce, the largest humanitarian pause of the war in that area. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 three more tankers damaged november 5 and ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump met his national security team and said iran would know soon enough; the nyt reports us forces are poised to resume major combat. iran sent a nuclear proposal via qatar to be discussed only after the us meets seven demands. democrats hold 54 seats. mississippi is within about 138 votes with roughly 3,600 mail ballots left and certification due november 13; alaska ranked choice results come november 18 while a doj suit seeks to block certification if peltola wins. melania trump hosted russian and ukrainian delegations (dmitriev and arakhamia) at the white house to mark the oleshky truce; more than 750 people were evacuated and russia refused an extension. trump met dmitriev and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks are set for november 10 to 11. yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet (arrested november 2) and henry constantín (jailed since september 16) remain held; rsf, iapa and amnesty condemned the detentions. law 186 was gazetted november 2 and takes effect november 9. still no attribution for the supermarket refrigeration hacks. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called the attacks deliberate; briefs.bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.
